LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Commanders, the full Week 10 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Commanders, the full Week 10 slate The Giants and Commanders played to a draw five weeks ago. Who wll win this time? | Getty Images Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants and Washington Commanders kick off Week 10 of the NFL season Thursday night at what promises to be a rainy, chilly MetLife Stadium. Can the Giants solidify their NFC East lead, or will the race for the division title tighten? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the Week 10 matchups. Which version of the Giants will show up on Thursday night? Will we get the sloppy Giants that came out flat against the Philadelphia Eagles, or the tough, physical, and technically sound Giants that showed up against the Houston Texans? John Harbaugh's 9-1 record home record on Thursday Nights is encouraging. I would say that this is a game the Giants should win on paper, particularly with Washington missing some of their best players and their starting center in the concussion protocol. However, I'm also not convinced that these Giants can play a normal game and just take care of business. I keep waiting for the Giants to play a complete game and execute on offense and defense, but this team seems unable to be both consistent and explosive. I hope the offensive line comes prepared to bully an injured Washington defensive line and J.J. McCarthy isn't forced into low percentage throws every third down by long yardage situations. Likewise, I hope that Dennard Wilson comes out swinging on defense, but also has a counterpunch ready in case Jayden Daniels has an answer to the Cover-0 blitz. I'm picking the Giants here, but they can't afford to take Washington lightly or give Jayden Daniels the chance to catch his breath and swing the game. Tony Del Genio This is the Giants' second consecutive must-win game. You wouldn't think that when 5-2-1 plays 2-5-1, but (1) the Giants haven't beaten the Commanders since Jayden Daniels became their quarterback (even though Daniels didn't play in one of those losses), (2) despite their record, Washington has beaten the Seahawks and only narrowly lost to the 49ers and Rams while the Giants were beaten soundly by the Rams, the only good team they've faced, and still have the 49ers and Seahawks coming up, along with the Jaguars and Lions. A division loss greatly weakens their hold on the NFC East lead, their only real path to the playoffs. Terry McLaurin is out for the season, but in his place is Stefon Diggs, who did not face the Giants in the first game. Jacory Crosky-Merritt, who beat the Giants' run D for a 33-yard TD right off the bat in the first game, is also out. The Commanders are further decimated by injuries since their last meeting to key starters such as DT Daron Payne and IOL Lucas Patrick. So really the Giants should prevail. The problem is…containing the running of Daniels, which they did not do well in their first meeting (103 yards, by far his highest of the season, and his only 2 rushing TDs of the season). Hopefully Dennard Wilson will have a plan for that. If so, and if the Giants execute it, then the Giants can win. David Hartman The rematch of the NFL's only tie game of the season will be played in prime time on Thursday night, and for the ninth time in nine games, the Giants are playing a team that doesn't have a winning record. But you can throw the records out the window: The 5-2-1 Giants, at home, are just 1.5 point favorites over the 2-5-1 Commanders. Go figure… Big Blue won with defense and a strong kicking game on Sunday in Philadelphia, with Arvel Reese perhaps becoming a star in real time. It was an ugly win, with the offense producing just 19 points. The Giants will need more than that against Jayden Daniels and company on Thursday night. Cam Skattebo is expected back, and that's good news. New York couldn't run the ball on Sunday, which stagnated their offense. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) might miss this game, however, and the O-line struggled at Philadelphia as it was. J.J. McCarthy wasn't terrible on Sunday, but he wasn't especially good either and now he's dealing with a hip pointer. Jameis Winston led New York on its only touchdown drive while McCarthy was temporarily knocked from the game. McCarthy hasn't thrown a TD pass (or an interception) in either of his two starts. This figures to be a close game, just like the first one. It'll be fun to watch standout rookies Reese and Sonny Styles — college teammates at Ohio State last season — leading the way for each defense. Seriously – how did anyone score on the Buckeyes? Anyway, Dennard Wilson needs to find a way to keep Daniels from gashing his defense with his legs. He ran for 103 yards and two scores in the first game. This game could come down to intangibles like turnovers and special teams. The G-Men have been winning (or tying) close games and that's a reflection on good coaching to a degree, and favorable luck. In a game that should be close, who am I to pick against that? Pick: Giants in a squeaker Valentine's View We are not picking games by the spread here, but I am surprised the Giants are just 1.5-point favorites. That indicates a continuing lack of real belief in the Giants in the betting market. The Giants understand the opportunity they have in front of them, and how important this game is. In the rainy, windy, miserable conditions at MetLife Stadium Thursday evening I think you have to expect what has become a typical Giants game this season — close, somewhat sloppy, decided by who makes the plays and who properly handles the situations at the end of the game. I have far more faith in the Giants to do that than I do the Commanders. We all remember the Commanders stunning clock mismanagement at the end of the Week 5 tie with the Giants. That sort of questionable decision-making has continued to plague Washington, which is 1-3-1 in games decided by one score. If you could the Arizona game, which I do since it was decided on the game's final play, seven of the Giants eight games this season were one-score games. The Giants are 5-1-1 in those games. They have lived on the edge, and have shown an ability to survive. Is that formula sustainable forever? Maybe not. It does, though, make me feel good about the Giants' chances on Thursday. away.blurb: Washington Commanders Rule Out 2 Players Ahead of Thursday's Giants Game Washington has ruled out two players. Starting center Lucas Patrick will miss the game with a concussion, while tight end Colson Yankoff will sit out with a knee injury. As for wide receiver Treylon Burks , whose status remained uncertain because of a foot injury that kept him out last week, he no longer carries an injury designation and will return to the Commanders' offense. Outside linebacker Malik Harrison is the only player still carrying an injury designation. He's questionable with a groin injury, and the Giants will likely determine his availability closer to kickoff. Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. The Washington Commanders are gearing up for arguably their biggest game of the season so far on Thursday night. They will travel to MetLife Stadium to take on the NFC East-leading Giants in a primetime matchup. The Commanders enter the game with a 2-5-1 record, while the Giants sit on the opposite end of the spectrum at 5-2-1. Both teams have a tie on their records after playing one another in a wild overtime finish a few weeks ago. Now, they meet for the final time this season, and if the Commanders want any chance of closing the gap in the division, this could very well be a must-win game. Both teams released their final injury reports on Wednesday. Although Washington has already dealt with a handful of season-ending injuries, the team has a fairly clean outlook heading into Thursday night. Neither player practiced at all this week, so these absences haven't caught Washington off guard. Nick Allegretti is expected to take over for Patrick at center. home.blurb: Washington Commanders Rule Out 2 Players Ahead of Thursday's Giants Game Washington has ruled out two players. Starting center Lucas Patrick will miss the game with a concussion, while tight end Colson Yankoff will sit out with a knee injury. As for wide receiver Treylon Burks , whose status remained uncertain because of a foot injury that kept him out last week, he no longer carries an injury designation and will return to the Commanders' offense. Outside linebacker Malik Harrison is the only player still carrying an injury designation. He's questionable with a groin injury, and the Giants will likely determine his availability closer to kickoff. Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. The Washington Commanders are gearing up for arguably their biggest game of the season so far on Thursday night. They will travel to MetLife Stadium to take on the NFC East-leading Giants in a primetime matchup. The Commanders enter the game with a 2-5-1 record, while the Giants sit on the opposite end of the spectrum at 5-2-1. Both teams have a tie on their records after playing one another in a wild overtime finish a few weeks ago. Now, they meet for the final time this season, and if the Commanders want any chance of closing the gap in the division, this could very well be a must-win game. Both teams released their final injury reports on Wednesday. Although Washington has already dealt with a handful of season-ending injuries, the team has a fairly clean outlook heading into Thursday night. Neither player practiced at all this week, so these absences haven't caught Washington off guard. Nick Allegretti is expected to take over for Patrick at center. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch the game Imagn Images The New England Patriots and Detroit Lions are headed to Germany this week. The teams will kick off Sunday's action with a 9:30 a.m. game at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins . The victory extended their win streak to four games. Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings . The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers . In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11). The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East. Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to know Injuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Patriots defense got embarrassed last week, with arguably Christian Gonzalez's worst game of his career. New England's defense has allowed the eighth most passing yards per game (231.9). The team does significantly better against the run, landing eighth-best (96.7), right behind the Lions' run defense (94.1). The Lions offense is top 10 in the league, thanks to Jaymyr Gibbs, who already has 847 yards on the ground and will present a challenge for the Patriots. The Lions' pass defense is still at the bottom in terms of yards allowed (260.9), and with the Patriots needing to improve and establish their air game, this would be the chance to try and expose Detroit's weakness. Pass game: The Patriots' passing game pales in comparison to their Week 10 opponent's. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has 61 receptions for 657 receiving yards, more than the Patriots' top two WRs ( DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism III ) combined. The lack of production is in part due to struggles from quarterback Drake Maye and the absence of a true WR1, with Brown missing most games and the loss of Kayshon Boutte this offseason. St. Brown's mom is from Germany and it will be the first game he plays on German soil, which should only increase his excitement and production. International history: This marks the sixth regular-season game to be held in Germany and the third played in Munich. It marks the final European game of the season. The NFL traveled to Germany last season as well, when the Colts and Falcons met in November at the Olympic Stadium. Detroit Lions president & CEO Rod Wood expressed his excitement to be playing in Germany, saying , "We are thrilled to be playing internationally and specifically in Munich for the 2026 season. As an organization, we have invested greatly in the German market and are excited to play in front of our passionate German fans." Lions vs. Patriots where to watch Date: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location : Allianz Arena (Munich, Germany) TV: Fox | Stream: fubo (free trial available) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Lions -2.5 ( via DraftKings ) Lions vs. Patriots prediction I think the Patriots will make some adjustments from last week and come out stronger in Week 10. This game could really go either way and we will know if the Patriots offense has the juice to win right away, as their first few drives tend to establish the rest of the game. If New England's defense can bounce back and Maye can stop giving the ball away, they can keep themselves in the playoff conversation with a win. The Patriots, which are off to a 5-4 start, are coming off a 45-27 defeat at the hands of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Meanwhile, the Lions, which are sitting at 6-2, defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, in their Week 9 tilt . New England – led by Mike Vrabel on the sidelines – has lost two of its last three games, including to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Additionally, it sits basically in the middle of the pack in both points scored (23.4/game) and points allowed (23.0/g). Yet, the Patriots still possess a myriad of talent on both sides of the ball. On offense, they're led under center by third-year passer Drake Maye, who has thrown for 18 touchdowns, 2,282 yards and a league-high 11 interceptions through nine games. He's coming off a three-interception performance against the Packers in which he completed a season-low 55.3 percent of his passes. Maye's top target this year has been veteran tight end Hunter Henry, who has amassed 32 catches, 361 yards and two touchdowns through the season's first nine games. Stevenson, a fourth-round pick of New England, has accumulated 399 yards and two touchdowns, and is presently averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Then, on the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots have received strong performances this season from the likes of EDGE defenders Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, cornerback Carlton Davis III and linebacker Christian Elliss. Ponder, a second-year pro , has already recorded 7.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and 13 QB hits, and has returned a fumble for a touchdown. And for his efforts, he's earned a 75.0 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the 23rd-best overall grade among 110 qualified players at the position. The Patriots will not, however, have the services of Davis (knee) for this Week 10 international affair. Plus, they will also be down starting left guard Ben Brown (knee), and are expected to be without Stevenson (knee). Plus, safety Kerby Joseph, who has yet to play a single game in 2026, will not be making his season debut in Germany. While both teams are rather significantly banged up, I still believe this matchup favors Detroit. At this present juncture, I believe the Lions have a 59 percent chance to secure their fifth straight victory. New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will not have a valuable weapon when the team takes on the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday. On Saturday, the Patriots announced that they have placed running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve. This comes one week after Henderson announced he had experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency." On October 29, the Patriots placed Henderson on the injury report with an illness designation. He has not practiced since. "Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days," Henderson wrote in a statement on November 6. "During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable." After Henderson released his statement, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the franchise will do everything it can to support him. " I'll support him, the best way that I know how is just to care for him, listen to him, and do whatever we can to get [him] healthy and get back, and to help this football team and to do what he loves." Henderson is in his second season with the Patriots. Last year, the 24-year-old finished third in Rookie of the Year voting after rushing for 911 yards and nine touchdowns. Henderson also caught 35 passes for 221 yards and one touchdown. This year, Henderson played in six games and rushed for 203 yards and one touchdown on 52 carries. away.headline: AJ Brown injury update as Patriots WR eyes international game return
away.blurb: A.J. Brown returned to practice for the first time in two weeks on Wednesday, Nov. 11 and has received an injury designation of "questionable" for Week 10. The designation is an indication that Brown could play in the game despite only practicing in a limited capacity all week. In Week 1, the former Eagle suffered a high ankle sprain and missed four games. Brown returned for two more games despite limited participation in practice. In Week 8, a knee injury was added to his status on New England's injury report, and he missed five more practices and two more games before his Nov. 11 return. Brown has now practiced three straight days – albeit in a limited capacity – and traveled with the Patriots to Munich. Brown is questionable to play in the Patriots' Week 10 game against the Lions . This week is the first that Brown has a status other than "out" since Week 7. The star receiver has missed New England's last two games while dealing with injuries to his ankle and knee. The Patriots' official website reported that Brown traveled to Germany with the team ahead of their matchup with the Lions in Munich. According to the team's injury report, he was a limited participant with ankle and knee injuries in all three days of practice leading up to Sunday's game on Nov. 15. New England also has one of its top other three receivers out on injured reserve: Romeo Doubs with a shoulder. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: A.J. away.headline: Patriots QB Drake Maye Calls Out Media Over Reports About Injured Teammate
away.blurb: Patriots QB Drake Maye Calls Out Media Over Reports About Injured Teammate - Newsweek U.S. News Patriots QB Drake Maye Calls Out Media Over Reports About Injured Teammate Published Surprisingly, previous reports indicated Stevenson would miss weeks due to an injury. However, the running back's recent appearance at practice raises the possibility of an earlier return, which could provide a major boost when the team faces the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, this weekend. During a press conference on Thursday, Maye addressed those previous reports about his teammate, calling out the media over the accuracy of its information. "I think that just speaks to, first off, the media not really knowing 100% what they’re talking about a lot of the time… [He’s] a guy that wants to be out there. Wants to be back for his team. … We’re in the midst of planning to make a run here and win a big one before the bye. So, this is a time for a lot of the players on this team to try and get out there, play with their teammates. [I know] that he’s a great player and he can help us out," Maye told reporters . Earlier this week, ESPN's Mike Reiss cited NFL insider Ian Rapoport, who reported that Stevenson was dealing with an injury to the back of his knee, and it was "expected to keep him out the next few weeks." ESPN's Reiss shared a video on Thursday showing Stevenson participating in drills off to the side after the team landed in Munich. As of this writing, he's still listed as "doubtful" on the team's injury report for Sunday's game. With the Patriots looking to bounce back from last weekend's loss to the Green Bay Packers, they can use all the help they can get. Wide receiver AJ Brown participated in Thursday's "jog-through" with the team, giving positive signs about his potential return from knee and ankle injuries. home.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
home.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." home.blurb: Wide receiver A.J. Brown was on hand for it. After missing back-to-back weeks due to a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September, the former All-Pro returned as a limited participant to begin Detroit Lions prep. But running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed among the sidelined in Foxborough and have officially been ruled out for the matchup in Munich. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) An illness that kept Henderson hospitalized for multiple days will now keep the running back out for a third straight game. The Patriots will be without another Brown on offense after the team’s starting left guard exited last Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. And in the secondary, a knee injury will also keep Davis from taking the field in Munich after he’d worked back from a neck injury throughout October. That leaves four non-participants from Wednesday potentially in play for the NFL international series. FB Reggie Gilliam (knee — IR return) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return) But a pair of 21-day practice windows are now open for New England along with one 53-man roster spot. After Van Roten headed back to practice last week, Gilliam did so to start work on the Lions. The fullback spent the past five games on injured reserve. He marks the fifth IR return designation utilized by New England. NFL rules allot eight per club. (Brett Davis/IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Pete Grathoff · Kansas City Star Sat, November 14, 2026 at 7:46 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A change was made at kicker ahead of the Chiefs' game Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta. Nope, it wasn't Harrison Butker getting benched or cut. The switch was from the Falcons, who released kicker Nick Folk earlier this week and signed Jake Moody off the Ravens' practice squad. Chiefs fans may recall that Moody briefly held a record when he made a 55-yard field goal for the 49ers in Super Bowl LVIII, but Butker nailed a 57-yard attempt in the next quarter. That remains the longest field goal in Super Bowl history. Will kicking be a factor in Sunday's game? Could Moody give Atlanta a, ahem, leg up on the Chiefs? Here is how 67 national experts see things playing out in Sunday's game, which starts at noon and will be broadcast on KCTV (Ch. 5). These picks were made before Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker was ruled out . A 28-21 Chiefs win is the prediction from the Sporting News' Bill Bender. This is from his story: "The Falcons have lost four of their last five games, and they have allowed 373.8 yards per game in that stretch. That's going to make things easier for the Chiefs, who have dropped their last two road games. Patrick Mahomes II has a 99.8 passer rating on the road." A 26-17 Chiefs victory is the call from the Associated Press' Rob Maaddi. Here is an excerpt from his story: "Patrick Mahomes has a new receiver after the Chiefs acquired Josh Downs. ... The Falcons have All-Pro running back Bijan Robinson, who leads the NFL with 880 yards rushing in one more game played than Walker." A 27-17 Chiefs win is the call from NBC Sports' Mike Florio. This is what he wrote: "The Falcons are capable of winning every game. It's just impossible to know when that version of the team is going to make an appearance." A 27-20 Chiefs victory is the outlook from the Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff. Here's what he wrote: "The Chiefs got back to what has done so well for them this season in the win against the Jets: Feeding Kenneth Walker III. It's a recipe that has proven to be a success this season." The Chiefs will win 26-10 , says the Los Angeles Times' Sam Farmer. This is from his story: "The Falcons pulled off a stunner against San Francisco three weeks ago but that was their Super Bowl." Picking the Chiefs are four of the five writers at NFL.com: Brooke Cersosimo (26-23 final score), Gennaro Filice (31-19), Bobby Kownack (28-21) and Dan Parr (26-21). Taking the Falcons is Jeremy Bergman (24-20). This is part of what Parr wrote: "In the last three weeks, Atlanta has allowed the most rushing yards per game (a whopping 190) and the most rushing yards over expected (182). Of course, a huge chunk of that production came courtesy of the Buccaneers' 324(!) rushing yards in a wet Week 8 tilt, but the Falcons allowed the previously dormant Bengals running game to churn out a season-high 123 yards last week (5.1 per carry) in Madrid." The defense had some major issues in that game. That will be the same here after the trade of safety Jessie Bates." picks.blurb: Falcons Roundtable: Jessie Bates Trade, Ian Cunningham's Deadline and Chiefs Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Christian Rauh · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 13, 2026 at 6:59 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Atlanta Falcons are looking to get back in the win column and keep their postseason hopes alive after losing their international game this past week against the Cincinnati Bengals. They now turn their attention to the Kansas City Chiefs, following a busy trade deadline for the Falcons new front office. On this week's Falcons Roundtable, the staff discusses the trades made at the deadline and how important this week's game is to getting back in the playoff picture. Following Atlanta's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati, what is your biggest concern about the Falcons? Michael Brauner: How much time do you have? The defense is not what we thought it was and Jessie Bates is now gone, the offense can't seem to find its identity and Michael Penix may not be the guy. It could get ugly the rest of the way if nothing changes. Christian Rauh: We've seen flashes of what Atlanta can accomplish, but they haven't been able to put together a complete performance. At some point, the Falcons have to stop making the same mistakes every week. Was trading Jessie Bates III the right decision, or should Atlanta have kept him? Michael Brauner: At the end of the day, as much as it stinks, this was absolutely the right decision. Getting legitimate draft capital in return for a safety who is getting older and on an expiring contract is always the right move, even if it hurts now. Christian Rauh: I don't love the decision to move on from Bates, but I understand it. The Falcons clearly have their eyes on the future, and getting draft capital back makes sense. However, replacing a player of his caliber isn't going to be easy, especially for a defense that already has plenty of questions. They did get some great value for him, though. What grade would you give Ian Cunningham for his first trade deadline with the Falcons? Michael Brauner: B+. There weren't many moves to be made, buying was out of the question, and they got real value for the guys they traded. Christian Rauh: B. It's clear he understands where this franchise currently stands and isn't afraid to make difficult decisions. Moving established starters isn't always popular, but Atlanta needs to build for the future. What must the Falcons do defensively to slow down Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on Sunday? Michael Brauner: This is not the same Chiefs offense from years ago. This is a unit who wants to run the ball and impose their will. Slow down Kenneth Walker, something few have done to this point, means slowing down this offense. Christian Rauh: It starts with getting pressure on Mahomes without allowing him to extend plays. Atlanta can't afford to give him time to sit in the pocket and pick apart the secondary. Is Sunday's game against Kansas City a must-win for Atlanta's playoff hopes, and who wins? Michael Brauner: .It is as must win as must win gets. Going into the bye week at 3-7 and losing three straight is pretty much season over. The NFC South is bad enough that perhaps they would still be alive, but on the brink. It's tough to have faith right now. Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Christian Rauh: Absolutely. At 3-6, the Falcons don't have much room for error if they want to remain in the playoff conversation. Unfortunately, I haven't seen enough consistency from Atlanta to believe they can knock off Kansas City. Chiefs 31, Falcons 17

They are each within one half-game of first place in their respective divisions. The Broncos lead Kansas City in the AFC West while the Falcons are looking up at the Panthers and the Saints in the NFC South. This despite Atlanta having lost two in a row and the Chiefs two of their last three. Kansas City is coming off a convincing 35-12 win over the New York Jets, a game that turned after the Chiefs trailed 12-7 in the second quarter. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both scoring passes going to Kenneth Walker III , who was the offensive centerpiece with 102 rushing yards, 143 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Travis Kelce added 72 receiving yards and even scored on a one-yard run. The defense took over after halftime, holding New York scoreless in the final thirty minutes as the Chiefs pulled away with 21 unanswered second-half points. Kansas City also went 4-for-4 in the red zone, an encouraging development after back-to-back losses to Seattle and Denver. Mahomes did briefly leave the field after hurting his arm/elbow on a strip-sack but returned and finished the game. As a result, the injury report is worth following as gametime approaches. Atlanta, meanwhile, returns home after a disappointing 34-17 loss to Cincinnati in Madrid, its second straight defeat following a 16-0 shutout loss at Tampa Bay. The Falcons opened strongly against the Bengals with an 80-yard drive resulting in a Michael Penix Jr. touchdown pass to Charlie Woerner . The scoring continued as they took a 10-7 lead later in the first quarter, but Cincinnati answered with 17 unanswered points in the second quarter and Atlanta never recovered. Penix finished 20-of-31 for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Bijan Robinson supplied the offense’s biggest bright spot with 100 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Drake London caught five passes for 68 yards, but Atlanta committed 12 penalties for 88 yards and allowed Joe Burrow to throw three touchdown passes. The central storyline from Atlanta’s perspective is will they be able to control the ball and keep Mahomes and co. off the field? The Falcons average 138.8 yards rushing per game. For Kansas City, it is about limiting Bijan Robinson and Atlanta’s rushing attack. The Chiefs have thrived against the run to date this season allowing just 96.3 yards on the ground per game. These teams last met two seasons ago. Mercedes-Benz Stadium was the site and Kansas City won 22-17. Mahomes threw for 217 yards and two touchdowns, while Rashee Rice caught 12 passes for 110 yards and a score; Atlanta, then quarterbacked by Kirk Cousins , had a chance late but could not complete the comeback. India, Nov. 14 -- Kansas City Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson is set to lead the team's rushing attack against the Atlanta Falcons in their Week 10 NFL 2026 matchup on Sunday, November 15. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported the development, confirming a major change in Kansas City's backfield plans after Kenneth Walker III suffered a groin injury during practice. The Chiefs are taking a cautious approach with their leading rusher, while rookie Johnson prepares for an expanded workload at Mercedes Benz Stadium in Atlanta. The development is particularly important for Kansas City because Walker has been one of the NFL's most productive running backs this season. His potential absence gives the rookie a chance to take on much bigger responsibility against a Falcons defence that must contain Bijan Robinson on the opposite side. Why Is Emmett Johnson Leading The Chiefs' Rushing Attack? The decision follows an injury setback for Kenneth Walker III, who reported groin tightness on Friday morning. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed Walker tweaked his groin and missed practice as the medical team assessed his condition. Reid also made it clear that Kansas City would not risk aggravating the injury. Schefter's latest update now puts Johnson at the centre of Kansas City's rushing plans for the Atlanta game. Who Is Emmett Johnson? Chiefs Rookie's 2026 NFL Stats Johnson is a rookie running back who joined Kansas City after playing college football at Nebraska. Here are his 2026 season numbers: Johnson also impressed during Kansas City's 35-12 victory over the New York Jets in Week 9, recording 34 rushing yards and a touchdown on six carries. His ability to contribute as a receiver could be particularly valuable if the Chiefs need to adjust their offensive approach against Atlanta. Kenneth Walker III Injury Update: Will He Play Against Falcons? The running back has enjoyed an outstanding first season in Kansas City, recording 872 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns in eight appearances. He is averaging 109 rushing yards per game, making him one of the most productive players at his position this season. Walker is also contributing in the passing game, with 26 receptions for 172 yards and four touchdowns. However, Andy Reid has indicated that the Chiefs will prioritise the player's fitness rather than risk a more serious injury. Facing off against the Atlanta Falcons , a win would put them right in lockstep with the Denver Broncos in the AFC West. Unfortunately, Kenneth Walker III will miss this weekend's matchup, as he deals with a groin injury he sustained at practice this week. It's a massive blow, but now rookie RB Emmett Johnson has a chance to prove himself. What's extra unfortunate about this injury is that Andy Reid has a chance to make NFL history if the Chiefs can rush for 150 yards. Facing a weak Falcons defense, especially against running backs, the Chiefs would seem to have a real chance at breaking this record for Reid in just nine games and 10 total weeks. However, with Walker sidelined, it's going to be a major uphill battle for the Chiefs' offense to run for 150-plus rushing yards. MORE : Harrison Butker keeps missing field goals and Chiefs fans have had enough Johnson has flashed for Kansas City this season, but having exciting moments here and there versus being a consistent runner is a major difference. The Chiefs are going to be relying on Johnson to lead this backfield, with Jaydn Ott potentially the No. 2 RB if he's active. Johnson running for 150 yards, even against a leaky Falcons defense, is a long shot. But if he can get close to 100, and Patrick Mahomes can add some through scrambles, and maybe a wide receiver or two gets a rushing play, this record might be in play. This is an interesting record for the Chiefs offense to chase on Sunday, as if they could pull it off, even without Walker, it would be quite the way to make this history. home.blurb: Falcons injury report: Zachariah Branch, Josh Woods, James Pearce Jr. held out of practice Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE From a health standpoint, Atlanta begins the week in relatively good shape. The Falcons placed defensive end Samson Ebukam and running back Brian Robinson Jr. on injured reserve last week, but they otherwise only had three players who were held out of Wednesday's practice due to injury, and one due to an illness. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch did not participate due to a hamstring injury that held him out of Atlanta's last game against Cincinnati; linebacker Josh Woods missed practice due to an ankle injury, and edge rusher James Pearce Jr. was held out with a back injury. Pearce made his season debut against the Bengals but was questionable leading into the game with the same back injury, which was a late development last week. Pearce played 15 snaps as part of Atlanta's defensive line rotation. Linebacker Divine Deablo, who played with his arm wrapped against Cincinnati, was limited on Wednesday. Additionally, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. was held out of practice with an illness. And it's a game for the Texans that'll be extremely important to take advantage of. They'll be taking the road trying to climb one game closer to .500, face up against another AFC Wild Card contender, and will be trying to build upon the 44-point outing they saw last weekend against the LA Chargers. So what can we expect from the Texans in this game against the Browns? Will they rise to the occasion for a second straight win, or fall into similar pitfalls that they have in their five losses so far this season? Well, let's sort through a batch of three bold predictions for the Texans to take our chances at guessing how things will unravel in Cleveland on Sunday: 1. The Texans are scoring a lot of points on a week-to-week basis, looking strong through their air attack thanks to some C.J. Stroud heroics , and they'll be looking to continue that trend in Week 10. This season has looked a whole lot different than 2025's output on the offensive side of the ball for Houston. The Texans are scoring a lot of points on a week-to-week basis, looking strong through their air attack thanks to some C.J. Stroud heroics , and they'll be looking to continue that trend in Week 10. The Browns, while they haven't allowed 30 points to an opponent dating back to Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, have certainly gotten close a few times. And on top of that, they haven't really played a high-powered offense like the Texans many times this season. If the Texans can keep their momentum through the air and the offense can continue to limit the penalties setting them back as they did last weekend, 30 points is wildly possible for this team. So far this season, the Browns are 0-1 in games where they allow 30 points or more, and have yet to score 30 points a game themselves. This might be a simple recipe for Houston's success this weekend. 2. And with that extra involvement, he turned in about as good of a performance as you could expect from him: four receptions on nine targets for 105 yards and a touchdown. Currently sitting at 3-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways long-term if they plan on making a postseason push in the AFC. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The good news? Sunday's matchup is on the road, a place where Houston is 3-1. The Texans will travel to Cleveland for a date with Deshaun Watson and the Browns in Week 10. Cleveland, which could be gunning for a wild-card berth under first-year coach Todd Monken, fell short on Sunday in a battle down in the bayou amid an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . Cleveland plans to start Watson, Houston's former franchise quarterback, but second-year passer Shedeur Sanders proved his potential by keeping the Browns alive in the Superdome. While throwing for nearly 200 yards and two touchdowns, Sanders was also sacked five times. Meanwhile, Cleveland's defense recorded five sacks, headlined by former Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger. "They're really good players, they're athletic and they're disruptive," Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley said. "They've got that speed off the ball. They use their hands and they play really hard continuously. They're a handful for sure." As for Houston, quarterback C.J. Stroud threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as Houston rolled past the Bolts in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. The Texans could be dealing with a multitude of injuries following Friday's practice. For the third straight day, rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge did not practice. Running back Woody Marks and defensive ends Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter also could be in trouble after missing practice on Thursday and Friday. How do the experts feel about Sunday's showdown between a pair of AFC dark horses desperate to pick up a win for different reasons? And knowing that Harrison Jr. is dealing with a hamstring issue, there's a possibility that the Texans' wideout suffered that hamstring tweak in the middle of Houston's team session on Wednesday, and will now be forced out for a period of time. However, for Anderson Jr., he deserves a bit more attention for his situation. He was a limited participant in practice on Thursday due to an ankle issue, and would inevitably not practice on Friday as a DNP. home.blurb: The Houston Texans already have a limited running game with Woody Marks taking a majority of their carries. The Texans could be without both David Montgomery and Marks following Thursday's injury report. Marks, who was not out at practice, was listed as limited with a knee injury on Thursday. Texans injury update: RB Woody Marks could miss Week 10 vs. Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Texans injury update: RB Woody Marks could miss Week 10 vs. Browns Cole Thompson, Texans Wire · Texans Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 8:49 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads What about having zero running game in Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns ? This is massive since Montgomery, the Texans' top running back in Week 1, has not played since the victory over the Tennessee Titans last month with a groin injury. Plus, given that the Texans waived running back Dare Ogunbowale earlier this week, the only running back left on the roster who's nearly 100 percent is Emari Demercado. Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley said that while Demercado hasn't seen an extensive amount of reps, running back's coach Danny Barrett always has someone locked in and ready to go. "Just getting them all ready, giving them opportunities and being conscientious of monitoring reps, who's gotten what reps, who hasn't, making sure we can get guys reps, really trying to format roles as the week goes on to allow those guys to just hone in and get time on task in specific things," Caley said. "We've got a good group of guys that all are there to support each other. Just trying to build it throughout the week and take it day by day, really." The Texans, who ranked 29th in rushing, could be in line for a strong day on the ground against Cleveland's defensive line. While the Browns have been successful in creating a pass rush, they rank 27th against the run, allowing 130.6 yards per game and 4.7 yards per run. Last week, Marks rushed for 70 yards on 12 carries and had his longest run of the season in a 44-22 win over the Chargers. Kickoff is scheduled for Noon on FOX. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Pittsburgh always seems to be right in the thick of it in these division games, and the first matchup was decided by only three points. I think the scoring margin is the same here, but with slightly lower scoring, in keeping with the trend of divisional rematches. … Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 20 Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) (MNF) Dajani ( Chargers +4.5): This is potentially the worst Monday night game of all time. A winless team that hasn't covered the spread since last year vs. a spiraling team starting a new quarterback. Jacoby Brissett is an upgrade over Joe Fagnano , but how much of an upgrade immediately? I don't have a great read on this matchup, but I'll take Jim Harbaugh to keep things close with his brother's old team. … Prediction: Ravens 20, Chargers 17 Dubin (Chargers +4.5): I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. … Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20 Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Da

It’s a critical game for both teams. The Packers remain in last place in the NFC North, even while winning five of their last six games. The Vikings have lost two consecutive games following a 6-0 start. Who will win the game? And, with this being the halfway point of the season, who will lead the team in rushing, receiving and sacks? And, ultimately, what will be the team’s final record and playoff fate? Here are our Packers-Vikings picks and midseason predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Vikings Prediction The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins this week. It’s a huge move for the Vikings, who somehow are 6-2 despite their quarterbacks’ inability to get the ball to Justin Jefferson. Cousins has faced the Packers 10 times while with the Vikings. He topped a 110 passer rating in seven of those games. OK, but what about this season? With the Raiders, Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards, second in touchdown passes and 11th in passer rating. Plain and simple, he remains a quality starting quarterback. Maybe I’m guilty of overvaluing Cousins. Maybe I’m undervaluing Jordan Love’s ability to consistently make plays against a Vikings defense that has won every matchup this season. Ultimately, I think Cousins will make one more big play, Love will be forced into one more big mistake and the special teams will get in the way. Score: Vikings 20, Packers 17 Bill’s Record: 7-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Vikings Prediction Yes, Kirk Cousins is back, but Green Bay's defense is for real until proven otherwise. The Packers had some answers for Brian Flores' group in Week 1 until Jordan Love was snowed under by Minnesota's pressure. This time, Lambeau Field will be the X-factor as the offensive line will be able to hear Love manipulate the line of scrimmage, which will help him make one more play than Cousins, as the Packers score a big win heading into their bye week. Score: Packers 21, Vikings 17. Jacob’s Record: 6-3. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) waits for the snap against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? Bill: 11-6 (Losses at home to the Vikings and Bills and at the Bears). Jacob: 12-5 (Losses at home against Buffalo and at Chicago). Where Will Packers Finish in NFC North? Bill: Last (with the same record as the Vikings but by losing the tiebreaker). Jacob: Second (Chicago wins the NFC North thanks to a win on Christmas Day at Soldier Field). Who Will Lead Packers in Sacks? Bill: Lukas Van Ness. I came up with this question in light of Micah Parsons’ presumptive return for the game against the Rams. Tucker Kraft has had a quiet season following last year’s torn ACL. It’s just part of coming off a major injury. So, while I thought about going with Parsons here, Van Ness will maintain the team lead and finish with eight sacks. Jacob: Lukas Van Ness. Van Ness has 4.5 sacks, which leads the team. His job should get a little easier with Micah Parsons' return to the lineup as he'll see less double teams. Parsons is a good bet here, as well, but has noted it may take him a while to look like himself again. The goal for the Packers is going to be to have him at his best in the postseason. Who Will Lead Packers in Rushing? Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) rushes the ball against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Jacob: Kaleb Johnson leads the team in rushing, which is incredible considering how his season has gone to date. The guess here is that he's out of Matt LaFleur's doghouse and going to be a more focal point of Green Bay's offense in Josh Jacobs' absence. That will continue even when Jacobs returns to the lineup. Who Will Lead Packers in Receiving Yards? Bill: Christian Watson has 879 receiving yards, putting him on pace to blow past 1,650 yards. Matthew Golden has 783 receiving yards, putting him on pace to push for 1,500 yards. I’ll take Golden to surge to the lead, though. He has five consecutive games of six-plus catches and four consecutive games with 10-plus targets. The sheer volume of passes going to Golden will push him past the explosive play off Watson, especially if last week’s game signals that his drops are behind him. The big question: Can they set the combined yardage record? Jacob: Christian Watson. This might be one of the most intriguing storylines down the stretch. Watson and Golden are neck and neck in this category now, with Watson holding a slight advantage. Watson is used to playing this late in the season and has made some big plays in big games. Golden has, as well, so this will be really close as the season comes to a close, but give us Watson to go over 1,200 yards for the season and earn the team's receiving title. Will Jordan Love Lead NFL in Passing Yards? Bill: Entering Sunday, Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow leads the NFL with 298.3 passing yards per game. Jordan Love is hot on his heels with a 290.9-yard average. That’s less than a first down per game. Playing five consecutive cold-weather games down the stretch isn’t going to help Love in his pursuit. Jacob: Yes, the only way the Packers can move the ball is on the right arm of Jordan Love. There's little reason to believe that's going to change, even when the elements start turning colder. Add in some games that could be potential shootouts, like a home game against Buffalo or a road game against Chicago. That could cause Love to pile up some big numbers. How Will the Season End? Bill: With the entire NFC North earning their way into the playoff field, the last-place Packers will squeak into the postseason as the No. 7 seed. It’s obviously a familiar place for the Packers. And it’s a death sentence. The No. 7 seed has to play at the No. 2 seed. If the No. 7 pulls off an upset, it will have to play at the No. 1 seed. So, let’s roll with the Packers upsetting the rival Bears in the wild-card round but meeting their maker against the playoff-rival 49ers in the divisional round. Jacob: The Packers will earn the NFC's fifth seed and have a date with the NFC South-winning Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first round of the playoffs. A big game from Jordan Love and Christian Watson, coupled with a suffocating defensive performance in which Micah Parsons will collect three sacks and a forced fumble against Baker Mayfield, will give the team its first playoff win since 2023. They will follow that by avenging last year's loss in the playoffs to the Chicago Bears by knocking them out at Soldier Field in the divisional round on a game-winning field goal from Trey Smack. That sends them to San Francisco, a house of horrors, for the NFC Championship Game, where the season ultimately will end with Brock Purdy leading a late touchdown drive to send the Packers into an offseason short of the Super Bowl. No team has ever blitzed as much as this year's Vikings, and they have blitzed Packers QB Jordan Love with even greater frequency. Now, the two teams will conclude their regular-season series with a chilly match at Lambeau Field. Vikings fans are still riding the excitement from a major adrenaline injection early this week as the team reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins via trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. What once looked like a potential beatdown in Green Bay now looks like a massive opportunity for the Vikings to end a two-game losing streak and sweep their biggest rival. There’s still a lot up in the air, especially since head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn't technically named Cousins the starter yet. But let’s be real: Cousins is starting unless there's a major setback . So, let’s dive into some predictions for Sunday, assuming “Kirko Chainz” makes his triumphant return. 1. Justin Jefferson returns to form (for real this time) Frick it, Justin Jefferson is down there somewhere. There is perhaps no larger beneficiary of the Cousins’ reunion tour than Jefferson. The seventh-year wide receiver is on pace to have the worst year of his career after poor QB play wrecked his 2025 campaign. Needless to say, it’s time for Jefferson to reclaim his spot on the wide receiver throne. Jefferson’s 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins far surpasses his 65 ypg average through six full games this season. Cousins’ mission on Sunday is simple: feed Jefferson. I’m predicting Jefferson will have a vintage performance with over 150 receiving yards and at least one touchdown. #Vikings QB Kirk Cousins says he saw Justin Jefferson today, and is excited to play with him again: “You don’t go chasing things, but you understand the player he is, and you go where your reads take you. You know he tends to make it right when you throw in his direction.” pic.twitter.com/zOoSnvilDO 2. Vikings defense holds the Packers to less than 20 points Green Bay’s 24 points per game ranks 12th-highest in the league through nine weeks, while Brian Flores and the Vikings defense are allowing a league-low 14.5 points per game to opposing offenses. Minnesota has held two of the league's best offenses, Detroit and Buffalo, to 19 and 23 points, respectively. This feat is even more impressive given the complete lack of help on the offensive side of the ball. “This roster has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing.” -Vikings GM Nolan Teasley on the decision to trade for Kirk Cousins pic.twitter.com/TkkJVs0fsp 3. Minnesota gets back in the win column This one is pretty straightforward: I have the Vikings righting the ship against a talented Packers team and ending their slide down the NFC North standings. While many had assumed star pass rusher Micah Parsons would be back by now, the Vikings have the distinct advantage of avoiding him in both regular-season matchups. Two of these teams will miss the playoffs pic.twitter.com/7VewNM4oiT With a reenergized offense, a motivated Cousins returning to the scene of a career-altering injury, and O’Connell in “prove it” mode, I think we finally see a well-rounded 2026 Vikings squad in action. away.headline: Packers appear built to withstand key injuries vs. Vikings in Week 10
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers are set to face the Minnesota Vikings in a game they must win to remain in the thick of the NFC North race . At 6-3, the Packers could move ahead of Minnesota in the division rankings if they come out on top. The Packers listed Xavier McKinney and Kevin Zeitler as questionable The Packers posted their final injury report for Week 10. Offensive guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps), safety Xavier McKinney (foot), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (back), Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), and running back Chris Moore (ankle) had the questionable designation. Now, just because they popped up on the injury report doesn't mean that they won't be available against the Vikings. That said, not having McKinney would be a huge blow. If the All-Pro safety isn't good to go, Kitan Oladapo may get the starting nod next to Evan Williams. However, the task became substantially tougher when the Vikes traded for Kirk Cousins. Compounding the issue is that Green Bay could be without a handful of key players. Oladapo logged 14 defensive snaps in the win over the New England Patriots when Evan Williams briefly left the bout . He has played a total of 28 snaps at safety that year, so you can bet Kirk Cousins could try to target him. The silver lining is that defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has done a good job of game-planning for Kirk throughout his coaching career , so he should have a trick or two prepared to stop the Minnesota offense. On the other hand, Green Bay should be able to withstand Zeitler's absence if he isn't good to go. If the veteran hog molly doesn't suit up, the Packers can easily plug in Laken Tomlinson at right guard and Aaron Banks on the left side. Granted, that's the lineup they've employed the past two games. Then again, the expectation was that after Zeitler made his debut against New England, he would see an uptick in playing time and possibly start at right guard. However, it looks like the coaching staff will have to halt the plan, as injuries have prevented him from hitting his stride since landing in Titletown in late September. Jordan Love gives the Packers the best chance to beat the VIkings Whether Kevin Zeitler starts or not, the Green Bay offensive line will be in good shape in Week 10. And that's the thing, if the Packers want to have a shot at beating Minnesota, they will need to keep Jordan Love upright. The Vikes have the top-ranked defense in the NFL. Sure, their run defense is 22nd in yards allowed, but can you truly trust Green Bay's underwhelming rushing attack to move the football? That means that it will be up to Love to put the team on his shoulders, and having a clean pocket will most definitely help.
