away.blurb: The 29-year-old quarterback could be targeting Minnesota's Week 12 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons for his potential return, according to Pelissero. Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is still "a couple of weeks away" from returning from his Grade 2 hamstring strain, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday. Murray's absence doesn't seem as urgent after the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a third-round draft pick. If Cousins misses time, the team will have to turn to Carson Wentz, who is serving as the backup in Murray's absence. Vikings Wanted Kirk Before Wentz's Struggles Mac Jones' Price too High for Vikings Murray suffered the injury during a 19-15 loss against the Detroit Lions in Week 8. He also missed Week 2 after suffering a concussion in Minnesota's regular-season opener. Although Murray compiled a 5-1 record as a starter this season, he was at the helm of a struggling Vikings offense. The eighth-year quarterback has just 1,022 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. Wentz struggled mightily when he stepped in for Murray on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. He completed just 32 percent of his passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions. Minnesota showed interest in reuniting with Cousins prior to Monday night , but Wentz' poor performance likely made it easier for the Vikings to name Cousins as the starter for a pivotal matchup against the Green Bay Packers in Week 10. Cousins is already familiar with head coach Kevin O'Connell's offensive system from the last two seasons of his six-year stint in Minnesota. He also has plenty of chemistry with star wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who enjoyed his most productive years on the receiving end of Cousins' passes. Cousins and O'Connell both struggled after parting ways, but they now have an opportunity to make up for lost time. Still, Murray's availability could prove valuable behind a 38-year-old quarterback. The silver lining is that defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has done a good job of game-planning for Kirk throughout his coaching career , so he should have a trick or two prepared to stop the Minnesota offense. On the other hand, Green Bay should be able to withstand Zeitler's absence if he isn't good to go. If the veteran hog molly doesn't suit up, the Packers can easily plug in Laken Tomlinson at right guard and Aaron Banks on the left side. Granted, that's the lineup they've employed the past two games. Then again, the expectation was that after Zeitler made his debut against New England, he would see an uptick in playing time and possibly start at right guard. However, it looks like the coaching staff will have to halt the plan, as injuries have prevented him from hitting his stride since landing in Titletown in late September. Jordan Love gives the Packers the best chance to beat the VIkings Whether Kevin Zeitler starts or not, the Green Bay offensive line will be in good shape in Week 10. And that's the thing, if the Packers want to have a shot at beating Minnesota, they will need to keep Jordan Love upright. The Vikes have the top-ranked defense in the NFL. Sure, their run defense is 22nd in yards allowed, but can you truly trust Green Bay's underwhelming rushing attack to move the football? That means that it will be up to Love to put the team on his shoulders, and having a clean pocket will most definitely help. If defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon and his unit, with or without Xavier McKinney, can generate enough stops and give the offense a couple extra possessions, the Packers should be able to earn their seventh win of the season. home.headline: NFL insider reveals Josh Jacobs injury return timeline for Packers after surgery
home.blurb: Green Bay Packers star running back Josh Jacobs suffered a fractured ring finger on his right hand during his team’s 45-27 beatdown of the New England Patriots this past weekend, leaving his availability in question. The injury required surgery, and now an update has emerged on Jacobs’ potential return for the Packers. According to Netflix NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Jacobs underwent successful surgery on his fractured ring finger on Friday in Los Angeles, with noted hand and wrist surgeon Dr. Steven Shin performing the procedure. Pelissero reported that Jacobs is expected to return to the Packers in the “next several weeks.” What George Pickens’ Bizarre Answer Means for His Cowboys Return vs. 49ers That could bode well for a Packers team that has won its last two games to improve to 6-3 this season in the competitive NFC North. Jacobs missed six games after being placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List amid a domestic dispute and the NFL reinstated Jacobs last month. However, his three games since returning haven’t been as productive as he or the team may have hoped. Jacobs recorded 36 carries for just 80 yards and one touchdown before suffering his finger injury against New England. More news: Lions HC Dan Campbell Reveals Major Drake Maye Concern Before Patriots Clash He’s been a key offensive component for the Packers for the past two seasons. He had 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns in his debut season for Green Bay, and then 929 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns last season. With Jacobs sidelined for the next several weeks, Kaleb Johnson could now take on a bigger workload for the Packers. Johnson has appeared in seven games, tallying 42 carries for 172 yards and one touchdown. MarShawn Lloyd has played in eight games for the Packers and has 149 rushing yards with two touchdowns to give Green Bay additional options at the position. Green Bay is heading into a challenging matchup this Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings, considered one of the league’s top defenses. The Packers’ running game could be important in taking pressure off quarterback Jordan Love. The Vikings also just added quarterback Kirk Cousins ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, potentially providing a significant upgrade for a struggling offense in the competitive NFC North. The Green Bay Packers face the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 15, beginning at 1 p.m. ET. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. away.headline: Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10
away.blurb: But what about Tate and four other major players missing the contest? That isn't even mentioning another questionable designation on, you guessed it, the offensive side of the ball. Robert Saleh's post-bye goal was for this team to come out swinging. On top of that laundry list, RB Tyjae Spears is once again questionable. Spears hasn't played since October 18, in the Titans' win over the Indianapolis Colts. Forgive our staff for entering tomorrow with a pessimistic mindset , but things simply aren't falling in a positive way for Tennessee. Of course, this doesn't negate the positive draft capital the team acquired at the deadline, nor does it cancel out Ward's progress. LB Cedric Gray missed Week 1 due to a concussion, and has still yet to return to the leading role he held last season. The Titans aren't 1-7 because of injuries, but setbacks like these have arguably led to the team ending up on the wrong side of the five one-score games they've lost. Carnell Tate Out vs. Jaguars: Why it's Bad News for Cam Ward, But Will Help Titans' Draft Process Carnell Tate missing the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 matchup wasn't enough to derail the offense from their best performance of the season. Even in a loss, Tennessee posted 36 points and ground up some real momentum for the first time in weeks heading into the bye. That in itself isn't the issue, but it's hard to really land a hit when you're missing a hand. The Titans, in addition to Tate, will be without LBs Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton, G Peter Skoronski, and P Tommy Townsend. The latter two were sent to the injured reserve list today. Titans are losing major players at the worst possible time This is a team coming apart at the seams at the worst time. One-instance absences - like Tate's in Week 8 - are easier to handle. But the Titans are a 1-7 squad down five starters against the best team in their division. However, it does mean that a Tennessee team down on their luck have caught another bad break. Tennessee can't catch a break this season You'll recall an 0-2 Titans team in a winnable situation on the road watching rookie RG Fernando Carmona Jr. exit vs. the New York Giants. Tennessee lost that game 12-7, and are just now trying to get Carmona back into the swing of things in practice. From that point of view, Week 10's injury report isn't all that surprising. Although, as the season winds down and certain decisions have to be made about this roster prior to an especially important draft, the added pressure from being down impactful talent works against the Titans' rebuilding process. We'll see how the undermanned team fares tomorrow, but for those hoping for a turnaround-sparking upset, you may want to splash cold water on that optimism ahead of time. These newcomers join a team that already holds a three-game lead in its division. They will also line up on the other side of the ball from an offense that is cooking with gas. The fourth-highest-scoring unit in the NFL has flat-out demolished half of its opponents. Trevor Lawrence , somehow, is still somewhat flying under the radar — probably because his offense keeps building such large leads that he does not need to rack up passing numbers in the second halves of these blowouts. Parker Washington has turned into a star, and Bhayshul Tuten emerged as a bona fide No. 1 running back. All of the pieces are in place. Just when it seemed like the Patriots were starting to put everything back together, they hit another rough patch. Just like they did to open the season, they have lost two of their last three games. The only win in that stretch was a five-point squeaker against the lowly Miami Dolphins . The road ahead does not get a whole lot easier with five likely playoff teams on the schedule over the next eight weeks. It is going to be a battle to return to the postseason after last year's run to the Super Bowl. Don't look now, but the Houston Texans are not out of it yet. The AFC South will remain out of reach so long as the Jaguars do not shockingly collapse, so it is Wild Card or bust for a squad that started the year at 0-4. At just 1.5 games back, the Texans are right in the mix. Since that winless first month of the season, the Texans have won three of four and took two of those games in blowout fashion. They just put up a season-high 44 points on the bottom-dwelling Los Angeles Chargers in a game that emphasized how far C.J. Stroud has come as a quarterback. He continues to play the best football of his career and is not even remotely the reason why the Texans are still two games under .500. Tank Dell's return to the wide receiver group and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s addition about a month ago also gave him a deep stable of pass-catchers to target, and he is cashing in. Losses are rare in the NFC North. At least one team has to add one to their tally in Week 10, though. The Packers are the only team with three losses, so every matchup means a little bit more to them as they try to work their way out of the shallow basement of the NFL's best division — one that could send all four teams to the postseason . They will have vengeance on their minds on Sunday as they seek to get payback for what the Minnesota Vikings did to them in a stunning second-half comeback in Week 1. home.headline: Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10
home.blurb: But what about Tate and four other major players missing the contest? That isn't even mentioning another questionable designation on, you guessed it, the offensive side of the ball. Robert Saleh's post-bye goal was for this team to come out swinging. On top of that laundry list, RB Tyjae Spears is once again questionable. Spears hasn't played since October 18, in the Titans' win over the Indianapolis Colts. Forgive our staff for entering tomorrow with a pessimistic mindset , but things simply aren't falling in a positive way for Tennessee. Of course, this doesn't negate the positive draft capital the team acquired at the deadline, nor does it cancel out Ward's progress. LB Cedric Gray missed Week 1 due to a concussion, and has still yet to return to the leading role he held last season. The Titans aren't 1-7 because of injuries, but setbacks like these have arguably led to the team ending up on the wrong side of the five one-score games they've lost. Carnell Tate Out vs. Jaguars: Why it's Bad News for Cam Ward, But Will Help Titans' Draft Process Carnell Tate missing the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 matchup wasn't enough to derail the offense from their best performance of the season. Even in a loss, Tennessee posted 36 points and ground up some real momentum for the first time in weeks heading into the bye. That in itself isn't the issue, but it's hard to really land a hit when you're missing a hand. The Titans, in addition to Tate, will be without LBs Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton, G Peter Skoronski, and P Tommy Townsend. The latter two were sent to the injured reserve list today. Titans are losing major players at the worst possible time This is a team coming apart at the seams at the worst time. One-instance absences - like Tate's in Week 8 - are easier to handle. But the Titans are a 1-7 squad down five starters against the best team in their division. However, it does mean that a Tennessee team down on their luck have caught another bad break. Tennessee can't catch a break this season You'll recall an 0-2 Titans team in a winnable situation on the road watching rookie RG Fernando Carmona Jr. exit vs. the New York Giants. Tennessee lost that game 12-7, and are just now trying to get Carmona back into the swing of things in practice. From that point of view, Week 10's injury report isn't all that surprising. Although, as the season winds down and certain decisions have to be made about this roster prior to an especially important draft, the added pressure from being down impactful talent works against the Titans' rebuilding process. We'll see how the undermanned team fares tomorrow, but for those hoping for a turnaround-sparking upset, you may want to splash cold water on that optimism ahead of time. home.blurb: The Jaguars are set to be without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III against the Titans as the Jaguars give them their bye week, while defensive end BJ Green will also be out as he works his way back from the injured reserve list. Tuten played in last week's game against the Baltimore Ravens despite not practicing that week with a foot/ankle injury, and he also sat out the first two practice days this week. He ended up getting 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown a week ago and did participate in Friday's practice as a limited participant, giving him the green light for Sunday against the Titans. The Jaguars had their third-worst rushing performance in terms of EPA/Rush during the 25-game Coen era on Thursday Night Football. Part of this had to do with execution, while another part of it had to do with a run-heavy second-half script after the Jaguars got up on the Ravens at halftime. Add in some bad weather that took the ball out of the hands of the passing game, and the Jaguars' rushing attack had the perfect storm for a regression game. As Coen said, there should be no long-term concerns. But in an AFC where the race for the No. 1 seed will be important week in and week out, and the Jaguars will need their running game to continue hitting its stride over the second-half of the season. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. The Dolphins won their first game on the road against the Jets a few weeks ago before losing to the Patriots and Lions at home. Meanwhile, the Colts have lost five in a row after back-to-back wins against the Texans and Commanders. It’s a low total at 38.5 between two lackluster squads, but somebody has to rack up some yards and find paydirt. Let’s take a look at a few prop picks, including an anytime touchdown scorer, for Dolphins vs. Colts on Sunday, Nov. 15. Best NFL Prop Bets for Dolphins vs. Colts Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jonathan Taylor Anytime Touchdown (-115) Daniel Jones OVER 0.5 Interceptions (-133) Caleb Douglas OVER 39.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Jonathan Taylor will play out the rest of the season in Indianapolis after the Colts elected to keep him through this week’s trade deadline. He’s one of the few offensive weapons for either side in this one, and feels like a good bet to score at this -115 price. After two weeks of not allowing a running back to score against the Jets and Patriots, the Dolphins yielded a rushing touchdown to Jahmyr Gibbs last week. They’ve also allowed the likes of Kenneth Walker and Christian McCaffrey to score multiple touchdowns against them. Taylor only has four touchdowns so far this season, but this is a game where he should be able to score once if not twice (2+ TDs is +550). Daniel Jones is also still in Indianapolis, for better or for worse. The quarterback has thrown just six touchdowns with 10 interceptions in nine games this season, getting picked off in eight of those contests. The Dolphins have four interceptions on the season, including one last week against Jared Goff. Given how often Jones has been picked off this year, Miami should be able to get another turnover against the quarterback this week. Caleb Douglas missed a few weeks due to an ankle injury, but has been solid since returning. In five games this season, the rookie has caught 19 of 27 targets for 296 yards. Douglas has gone OVER 39.5 receiving yards in four of his five games this season, only failing to do so in Week 2 against the 49ers. He’s racked up 70, 43, and 70 yards in three games since coming back from injury, and the Colts defense allows him a great opportunity to get to the 40-yard mark again. TOP Pick Dolphins vs Colts prediction: Under 38.5 This has all the makings of an ugly, low-scoring football game, and I'm perfectly fine investing in the Under. The Miami Dolphins aren't terrible defensively, either — ranking 13th in total defense coming into this one. Neither offense inspires much confidence, and when we're dealing with a total this low, the margin for error is razor-thin. Sustaining drives, converting third downs, and finishing in the red zone will be critical, and I'm not convinced either team can consistently check those boxes. Dolphins vs Colts combo There's a clear path for both running backs to see significant volume in this matchup. Seth McGowan has slowly been eating into Jonathan Taylor 's workload, clearing this number in two of his last three games. Meanwhile, Ollie Gordon has become the bell cow in Miami with De'Von Achane out of the picture, and with the Colts coughing up 137 rushing yards per game, there's plenty of runway for Gordon to get his share. I'm feeling warm and cozy here. We're not asking for anything crazy here. Just a slow, methodical football game. Under 38.5 points Ollie Gordon Over 61.5 rushing yards Seth McGowan Over 33.5 rushing yards Dolphins vs Colts touchdown scorer: Caleb Douglas Caleb Douglas has the speed and big-play ability to turn one touch into six, giving Miami a legitimate home-run threat against Indianapolis. He's emerged as the Dolphins' WR1 and go-to option in the passing game, averaging seven targets over his last two contests. With backup quarterback Kyle McCord under center, I'm expecting Douglas to be heavily involved early and often, giving him plenty of opportunities to find the end zone. Over the last month, our young Defense has been ascending on a really nice arc. I'm going out on a limb to say they play lights out this week and they win this game. Time for a Defensive touchdown and I say JRod or Johnson deliver. The Offense has the potential to be effective this week, even though we have no clue what we'll get from McCord. I think this OL hears the noise and criticism…so challenge them…run the ball, run it again, and run it some more. The Colts won't be able to hold up. Granted, watching paint dry is probably more exciting, but when you're coaching and developing a young team, you look for opportunities like this to challenge them to deliver. cyberflea has the woeful Colts sticking it to the Phins. McCord throws for over 300 yds and 3 TDs in relief of Willis as the Dolphins beat the Colts 31-17….not gonna happen. This was a winnable game for the Fins, not as much with McCord at QB and without defensive captain Sieler, although the former will hurt more. I figure this will be a pretty low scoring game especially for the Dolphins who are 31st in passing yds with Willis. A matchup of two of the worst teams in the NFL. The Dolphins offense will rely on their running game and short passes; the Colts know this and will game plan accordingly. The Dolphins may still be able to pull this one out with a big day on defense which must shut down RB Jonathon Taylor and force Daniels into throwing interceptions that result in short field situations. The Dolphins offensive line has to give McCord maximum protection which is possible since the Colts pass rush is weak. No chance if the Dolphins turn the ball over and continue their penalty dance party resulting in long yardage situations. One thing is certain is that the Dolphins great special team's unit cannot give up long returns to the Colts. Yes, I'm being sarcastic with "great". Shutting down Taylor will be the key; however Daniel Jones will be the difference factor despite a rough season, and the one-dimensional offense of the Dolphins will struggle with McCord as a first-time starter. I hate to be negative however; reality tells me that the Dolphins are going to go winless with McCord at QB. Colts win 20-6 Zen4Phins has a full list of predictions for you, with the Phins coming out on top. Interesting that people are saying it's not looking good for our offense with Willis out … this offense averaged about 14 points per game with Willis IN …. are we really losing a lot 🤔 phinette sees the defense holding up their end of the bargain and the offense letting us all down. We should match up fairly well against a really bad Colts team, but I have no faith in our offense for myriad reasons. I believe the defense will hold the Colts to 17 points, but I think we'll struggle to put up more than 10. Phoenix6 has Miami squeaking one out in a defensive battle. This has turned into an ugly game on the surface. Miami's down a QB, & Indianapolis has traded their good players. Both seem to be in another game. Which team gets the highest selection in the draft. I'm going with Miami's defense over Indy's offense in a thriller… 13, 10. Dr.Greenthumb sees a win as the biggest threat. This might be the most important game of the year to lose. Jets have the Colts 1st rounder and also need to draft a qb. A win here could have a catastrophic long-term impact. As a lifelong Fins fan, go colts. Pod of Dolphins is just going to vanish if things get ugly. This reminded me of a blind double date years ago with my buddy and two unattractive sisters in a bar, after 30 minutes I told them that I needed to go to the bathroom, to never return surfla8 sees something in all of those numbers. Kyle Mc Cord is #14. That's one better than 13. He's from Philadelphia. That other guy was from Pennsylvania also, but from a worse city. McCord finished 10th in Heisman voting in his final season in college. Dan finished 9th in his. See the numerology thing here? IDK if Kyle's the next Dan, but Dolphins will win by 1 this weekend. David7777 is ready to throw in the towel on this season. Think we should call up the entire practice squad this week and see how they play. Colts 27 Dolphins 3. Then we get our future QB when we sandbag the Chargers Game. JUK has a better feeling about this game before all of the injuries. Before Willis and Sieler went down I would have had this the Fins as big favorites for this one. I still think they will probably win, because you cannot underestimate the importance of mentality in sports. Every single member of the Colts locker room knows their top brass have completely checked out on this season, and that has an impact. They will play for pride, but the message is very clear- we don't believe in you and we're thinking about the future. The fins are bought in. Our offense has struggled against elite pass rushers (colts don't have any) and dominant interior forces (Buckner was their guy and he is gone). I expect us to be able to run the ball, and that gives McCord the chance to be a caretaker. If Willis was healthy I'd have forecast his best game of the year CluelessNFLfan thinks Taylor is the difference-maker in this one. Too bad the Colts didn't trade Taylor yesterday. I just can't see us winning this game. ImRightYoureWrong says don't bother! Colts 7, Dolphins 5 Don't bother watching MiamiItaliano says this is our best chance for a win until late December McCord has a decent game, 200+ yards, 1 TD, no picks. Dolphins defense holds Taylor to less than 70 yards rushing. Dolphins win by 3. This is about as good of a chance they get to win until the Chargers game. Well, the consensus seems to be that there's not much hope, especially with Willis out. At this point, I guess we should all focus on whatever development we can get out of these rookies to carry over to next season. Well, technically. The Colts, 2-7, could claim the top spot, but they do not own their own first-round for the next draft, with the New York Jets holding that selection as part of an in-season trade last year that sent cornerback Sauce Gardner to Indianapolis. Despite the Dolphins' positive signs of growth over the past several weeks, the oddsmakers have given the Colts a slight nod in this game. The FanDuel Sportsbook line opened with Indianapolis favored by 2.5 points , slightly under the typical three-point advantage given to a home team, and it has remained steady as of Tuesday morning. The point total is set at 40.5, while Miami is +116 on the money line for the straight-up win. The Colts are -136 for the win. This week could see massive changes in odds as Tuesday's trade deadline approaches. Indianapolis is expected to be sellers today, with running back Jonathan Taylor considered one of the top available players on the market, and rumors swirling around defensive tackle Grover Stewart and quarterback Daniel Jones. If the Colts do start making trades ahead of the 4 p.m. Eastern deadline, how will the line move? Miami could also be sellers, with teams reportedly interested in players like linebacker Jordyn Brooks and defensive tackle Zach Sieler. The Dolphins may not be eager to move on from core pieces of their rebuild, but they may be offered a package of draft picks they cannot refuse. Tuesday could significantly affect the odds for this weekend's game, but for now, the Colts are slightly favored.

away.headline: Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report
away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. Wright has been dealing with a quad injury that led to him being ruled out in Week 9. Now, he is set to return against the Colts. Brewer has now missed his second straight practice, as he is currently in concussion protoco l. It is not unlikely that he will suit up against the Indianapolis Colts. The full injury report is as follows: Running back Kaytron Allen (quad), safety Michael Taaffe (wrist), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and running back Jaylen Wright (quad) were all full participants yet again. Despite the semblance of a laundry list of injured players, the Dolphins look to be in decent shape. Losing Brewer will be a huge hit to the offense, but Andrew Meyer will be there to step in. Meyer spoke on Thursday about not only learning from "the best center in the league" but also stating that he has the confidence to step in for the Miami offensive line if that is what happens. The Dolphins are looking for their second win of the season, as they will face the struggling Colts. Indianapolis may not be a pushover opponent, but they also got rid of many players at the trade deadline, leaving this to be a potential "easier" matchup for Miami.

away.headline: Dolphins-Colts Game Preview and Predictions: Can Miami Overcome Injuries?
away.blurb: That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. Analysis: This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. For a change, the Miami Dolphins are given a chance by more than just one or two national media members heading into their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts — and that's despite the injury to starting quarterback Malik Willis. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. away.blurb: Reagor being elevated would seem to indicate that wide receiver Chris Bell indeed will be inactive after being listed as doubtful on the final injury report of the week with a knee injury that kept him out of practice Thursday and Friday. Along with potentially getting snaps at wide receiver, Reagor also becomes an option to return punts and/or kickoffs. Bell will be joining Jalen Wayne, who was ruled out Friday, on the inactive list. Reagor will join Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas, Kevin Coleman Jr. and Jalen Tolbert on the game-day roster. Lastly, as expected, the Dolphins didn't activate cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. off PUP and officially was downgraded to out on the injury report. The Miami Dolphins made the expected moves Saturday ahead of their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts, but they still have an opening to be filled at some point. The Dolphins announced early Saturday afternoon they had signed kicker Zane Gonzalez to the 53-man roster off the practice squad, along with elevating quarterback Brady Cook and wide receiver Jalen Reagor. Head coach Jeff Hafley already had indicated earlier this week the team would be signing Gonzalez to the active roster, which was the only way he could kick again for Miami this season after exhausting his three allowed elevations. The move can be questioned based on Gonzalez missed a field goal each of the past two games, although special teams coordinator Chris Tabor said Thursday the miss against the New England in Week 8 was more about the whole operation than a Gonzalez mistake. "I think he's a good player," Tabor said. "I think he's a player that, yes, he missed a kick he should have made. We can all agree about that and Zane would too. In my eyes, that's kind of his first miss. I know on stats that it's two, sometimes there's other things that go on. I'm just not really, I'm not a guy that just pushes players away. He's been on the street for six weeks, seven weeks, and this was his third week back, so I think that he's still working to get to where he needs to be, right? I got a lot of confidence in him and we're working hard at getting better. I look forward to watching him kick this weekend. I got a lot of confidence in him, and it's real easy for me." The signing of Gonzalez put the Dolphins at 52 players on the active roster after the moves this week that saw QB Malik Willis and DT Zach Sieler go on injured reserve, CB Reese Taylor getting waived, and DT Keith Cooper Jr. signed off the Carolina Panthers practice squad. Cook was on the active roster earlier this season before being waived and re-signed to the practice squad, and he seemed like a logical choice to be re-signed to the 53 if he's going to back up new starter Kyle McCord for the next four games while Willis is on IR. Technically, the Dolphins don't have to make that decision until after Cook has been elevated three times, which woud come after the Week 12 game against the New York Jets. away.headline: Dolphins Lose More Key Starters to Injury as Concerns Mount
away.blurb: Despite Miami's 1-7 record, this game appeared to be very winnable for a Dolphins team that had played more competitive football recently. After a win over the New York Jets, the Dolphins fought hard games against the playoff-hopeful New England Patriots and Detroit Lions. While Miami came out on the losing end in both games, there were signs of encouragement. Unfortunately, after the game against the Detroit Lions, Miami's depth will be considerably tested. Earlier in the week, the Dolphins placed team captains Zach Sieler and Malik Willis on injured reserve. While Willis could return after four weeks, Sieler was declared out for the season. Hafley also announced discouraging news on rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. The rookie wide receiver appeared on the injury report on Wednesday with a knee injury as he was a limited participant in practice. Bell then missed the remaining two practices of the week. Hafley announced that Bell will be doubtful for Sunday's game. Hafley added of Bell , "Chris got hit in his knee. The same knee, but has nothing to do with his surgery. So nothing long term, like I said. He's doubtful, but I don't foresee this – we'll see if he can go Sunday, but has nothing to do with his (prior) injury." NFL.com 's crew of five writers all picked the Colts to come out victorious over the Miami Dolphins. Brooke Cersosimo predicted the Colts would win 16-13. home.headline: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts
home.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
home.blurb: Wide receiver Chris Bell has been limited in practice this week with a knee issue. Hafley said he would not practice on Friday and is doubtful, but he has not been ruled out. Hafley said Bell got hit in the leg during practice and it did not have to do with his prior knee injury. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. The Panthers will be experimenting a bunch this week. They’ll presumably shake the personnel up along the offensive line, and they’ll have a new defensive coach calling plays. Such risks might work out for them, kind of like how their RPOs stunned the Lions’ defense on Sunday Night Football (gosh, that feels like a lifetime ago!). Even still, I think the Broncos are too talented on defense and too disciplined on offense to let a winnable game like this slip away. Sunday, they’ll want to steady the ship. And they will have to pull off an upset to do so. The Panthers (3-4) still sit atop the NFC South, but in order to hold onto their station, they’ll likely need to emerge from Bank of America Stadium with a victory against one of the powers of the AFC — the Denver Broncos (6-2). The Sean Payton-led team has won its last four contests, including a 28-24 thriller against the Chiefs. Another flattering Broncos stat: They’re 15-0 in their last 15 regular-season one-score games . The Panthers are 3-4 against the spread so far this season. The Broncos are 6-2. Broncos head coach Sean Payton has a long history in the NFC South. That included a Super Bowl in New Orleans. Payton’s record against the Panthers, according to Pro Football Reference, is 19-13, including the only win as Broncos head coach against the Panthers in 2024. home.headline: Travis Etienne Jr. Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Saints RB's Return Timeline from IR
home.blurb: Etienne had been out of action since suffering a hamstring injury during a Week 3 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. The Panthers represent a soft landing spot for Etienne should he indeed return to the lineup on Sunday, as they rank 28th in the NFL against the run this season. New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr.'s five-game absence reportedly may come to an end Sunday. According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the Saints plan to activate Etienne from injured reserve, putting him in line to play against the NFC South rival Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon. ▶️ Full Raiders-Saints Recap 05:42 After racking up 1,399 total yards from scrimmage and 13 touchdowns with the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, Etienne cashed in by signing a four-year, $47.4 million contract with the Saints in free agency. Sharing the backfield with Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller, Etienne was off to a relatively slow start through his first three games with New Orleans, rushing for 128 yards and no touchdowns on 30 carries, while also catching 11 passes for 51 yards. While Etienne was not being used as an every-down back, his efficiency was solid, averaging 4.3 yards per carry, which matched the second-best average of his career from last season. The 27-year-old Etienne is now set to rejoin what remains a crowded backfield with Kamara and Audric Estimé in the mix. Miller was released by New Orleans last week. It would be fair to expect head coach Kellen Moore to re-integrate Etienne slowly given the nature of the injury he is returning from and how much it can impact a running back. home.blurb: The Carolina Panthers ' defensive blueprint for their Week 11 matchup against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday could require adjustments following the latest update on outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips . After participating fully in Wednesday's practice, the pass rusher was downgraded to limited on Thursday's injury report because of his lingering hamstring issue. Although Phillips' full participation on Wednesday appeared encouraging, that session was only a walk-through, making Thursday's limited designation a more telling development. Phillips was not the only starter whose practice status changed Thursday. Left guard Damien Lewis (knee) also went from full participation to limited, while linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) was the only player who did not practice. Cornerback Will Lee III (hamstring), who missed last week's game, returned to full participation, as did starting cornerback Mike Jackson (groin). The Panthers will be hoping Phillips can return soon, given the difference his pass-rushing production could make to their defense. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. Regardless, if the Jets don't exit next week with their eighth loss of the season it will be a major surprise. Join Gang Green Nation on game day! picks.blurb: Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 04: Running back Ray Davis #22 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. The Bills defeated the Jets 35-8. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Jets will be a home underdog against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, having lost seven of their last eight games. Other than a last-gasp loss to the Patriots in week four, the Bills' record is unblemished this year. Surely the Jets can't pull off an upset, can they? Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to flip their season on its head: It's a trap! America is already looking ahead to the Bills-Chiefs game scheduled to take place in the evening of Thanksgiving Thursday. While Buffalo has two games to play between now and then, they will feel good about their chances of still only having one loss after playing the Jets this week and Miami next week. Kansas City has lost just twice so this could be decisive in the race for the AFC's top seed. We've seen situations like this before though. While the Jets are rarely the team to take advantage of the opportunity, their profile as a team that has kept a lot of games close and come up just short in the end could make them dangerous if the Bills get complacent. And if they did get complacent, who could blame them? After all, the last time these teams met, the Bills rested all of their starters and still won 35-8. Then again, that was a very different Jets team too. The only current non-offensive line starters who started that game are Harrison Phillips, Jamien Sherwood and Adonai Mitchell. Can Mitchell bounce back? It's become traditional this year to have at least one high profile player that doesn't get the ball on offense. Last week, it was Adonai Mitchell, a player who seven days earlier, had posted the best numbers of his career. The Jets really seem to be struggling with the whole "many mouths to feed" aspect of having provided their quarterback with an adequate number of pass catching weapons for the first time in several seasons. However, Mitchell not seeing the ball last week was not for the want of trying as he was thrown to seven times. Opening drive success We could easily spend column inches here talking about why the Jets can't convert in the red zone, or how they shouldn't abandon the running game, or when are they ever going to intercept another pass, but how about we discuss something they have actually been doing well? For each of the past five games, the Jets have driven downfield and scored on their opening possession, which has played a big part in them still being competitive heading into the second half of each game. So, now we have to ask the question – can this continue? And…how will the team react if it doesn't? This isn't the first time in recent memory that the offensive has looked good early on in games, and executed the scripted part of the gameplan effectively, only to then go on to struggle in the second half when points are needed to convert wins. Back in 2020, where Adam Gase's Jets were in danger of going winless until very late in the season, they actually scored eight times in a row on their opening drive. The current decision makers would ideally not like to have too many similarities to that 2020 team. Gregory Rousseau's ascent to super-stardom The biggest threat on the Bills defense is obviously edge rusher Gregory Rousseau, who is having a monster year. After just eight games, Rousseau has already tied his career-high with eight sacks, while also doubling his career mark for passes defensed with another eight. Rousseau primarily lines up on the left, so it will be mostly up to Armand Membou to try and keep him quiet. Rousseau had a two sack game against the Jets in his second season in 2022, but surprisingly otherwise only has one sack in eight other games against the Jets. The Bills are 7-2 in these matchups, though. Having not been traded, is Will McDonald's role going to change? The Jets opted not to trade former first round pick Will McDonald during the week, despite reports of interest from a number of teams. Head coach Aaron Glenn has been suggesting McDonald is still very much in the Jets plans for the rest of this season, and he is of course under contract for next year after New York exercised his fifth year option. He even implied McDonald had earned a bigger role. McDonald's defensive snap count percentage has dropped from 66% in both 2024 and 2025 to just 46% in 2026 and, even more confoundingly, his percentage of run snaps has increased. Will an increase in playing time for McDonald happen on Sunday? And, if it does, are we destined to see diminishing returns in regard to his production? What's the plan for the secondary? A matchup against the team with the number one offense in the entire NFL is not really the ideal time to experiment with line-up changes but the Jets are desperately striving for more consistency from their back seven, in addition to having an undermanned front that is struggling to stop the run. Having missed a meeting and made some on-field mistakes, the previous starting slot corner – Jarvis Brownlee Jr. – is in the doghouse. However, rookie D'Angelo Ponds has looked overmatched at times which is hardly surprising given how he is learning a new position and missed half of training camp. New York also experimented with using Minkah Fitzpatrick in the slot on Sunday, elevating Malachi Moore into the lineup at safety for basically the first time all year. Could this be the answer? Time will tell. Let us know how you see things going in Sunday's game in the comments section…

away.headline: Buffalo Bills Handed Concerning Injury News on $72M Starter
away.blurb: Buffalo Bills Handed Concerning Injury News on $72M Starter Unlock the latest Heavy on Bills news — direct to your inbox. The Buffalo Bills could be without an impact starter on Sunday against the New York Jets . Buffalo's offensive line has been hindered by injuries as of late. Starting right tackle Spencer Brown missed the game two weeks ago. Then, last week, starting left tackle Dion Dawkins and starting left guard Alec Anderson were inactive due to injuries. The Bills will now go on the road to play the Jets on Sunday. Buffalo Bills Get Concerning Injury News on Spencer Brown Bills get injury news on Spencer Brown. Buffalo got Brown back from injury last week but he once again could be inactive on Sunday. Brown is in the midst of a four-year, $72 million deal and is a key part of the offensive line. However, he's been on the injury report again, and The Athletic's Joe Buscagalia believes it's unlikely he will be playing on Sunday. "Starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who has been trying to play through a back injury he suffered against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, was not on the practice field at all. … Brown suffered an ankle injury early in Monday's game and gutted through the rest of the evening. After practice, Brown was in the huddle with his teammates, but he was in sandals with a big wrap on his right ankle," Buscagalia wrote . "It wouldn't be stunning if they are playing the long game to give him rest for the back and ankle injuries, given his importance and the Bills' being on a short week. They also have another short week on the horizon, taking on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 12 on Thanksgiving with only three days after their Week 11 game against the Miami Dolphins. Resting Brown could be important. Missing Thursday's practice is usually not a good sign." If Brown can't go, Tylan Grable will start at right tackle again. Grable replaced Brown two weeks ago and started at left tackle a week ago. Given that Buffalo is a huge favorite, resting Brown makes sense to make sure he's healthy for the stretch run. Although the Bills are massive favorites against the Jets, Buffalo isn't overlooking them. Bills head coach Joe Brady believes the Jets pose a challenge for them on defense. So, they have to be smart with the football. "When you look at it, you can get caught up in the records, but the records, I think, always lie to you in the NFL; that's why you never can focus on them," Brady said . "I think it's a really good offense that has been in a lot of games, and there's a lot of one-score games, and you take a couple plays here and there situationally, and the record looks completely different, and people are probably talking about the Jets a little differently. "So it's going to be a huge challenge for us defensively as a football team and a great opportunity for us." The Bills are 8.5-point favorites on the road against the Jets. Buffalo's first injury report of Week 10 includes six limited participants and five full participants. picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved Seahawks vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Chris Spiering, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Seattle Seahawks have a golden opportunity to make a statement against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10. Seattle is coming off a quieter offensive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, but this matchup presents a chance for the Seahawks to get back on track in a big way. The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. Meanwhile, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first NFL start against a Seattle defense that has been one of the toughest units in the league. I expect the Seahawks to take advantage of both matchups. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 4: Jadarian Price scores his first NFL touchdown Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images This could finally be the game when Jadarian Price gets into the end zone for the first time in his NFL career. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. JSN is coming off a relatively quiet performance against the Cardinals, finishing with seven catches for 51 yards without a touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. away.blurb: As for Milroe, the first-team repetitions are a chance to show he can handle more than a limited package constructed around his athleticism. Seattle will start Lock against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 15, with Darnold ruled out because of quadriceps and rib injuries. The veteran has been limited in practice while managing an elbow injury and the oblique issue he suffered against the Arizona Cardinals. Klint Kubiak Speaks out on Facing Seahawks in Week 10 Seahawks' Mike Macdonald Gives Strong Jalen Milroe Statement Amid QB Injuries Unlock the latest Heavy on Seahawks news — direct to your inbox. The Seattle Seahawks have spent the past two weeks dealing with injuries to their top two quarterbacks. That's given Jalen Milroe more time with the starting offense. And head coach Mike Macdonald likes what he has seen. Speaking with reporters Friday, Nov. 13, Macdonald delivered strong praise for the second-year quarterback's work while Drew Lock and Sam Darnold recover from injuries. "I think it's appropriate to say Jalen has done a tremendous job when he's been in there with the ones," Macdonald said. The coach went on to laud Milroe's work ethic, accuracy and decision-making. He specifically highlighted the young quarterback's ability to deliver throws on time. It's a welcome assessment for a player who has waited for a chance to show his ability for much of his NFL career. Seahawks' Jalen Milroe Impresses Mike Macdonald With First-Team Offense Milroe has taken snaps with Seattle's starters during the past two weeks as Lock works through elbow and oblique injuries. Macdonald made it obvious Friday that the extra work hasn't been wasted. The coach described Milroe as decisive with the football and praised his execution when called upon to replace Lock during practice. The comments came in a Nov. 13 report from Seahawks.com's John Boyle . Seattle selected Milroe in the third round of the 2025 NFL draft, taking the former Alabama quarterback with the No. 92 overall pick. His rookie season showed very little game experience. Milroe appeared in three regular-season contests, carrying the ball three times for four yards without attempting a pass. Heading into 2026, he sat behind Darnold and Lock on the depth chart The latest injuries have changed his practice workload, though they haven't produced an official quarterback change. Seahawks Have More QB Questions Before Raiders Game Lock is also feeling his own physical problems. Still, Macdonald put forth confidence Friday that Lock can handle another start, so Milroe is an important insurance option. If Lock cannot finish Sunday's game, Seattle could be forced to turn to the former Alabama standout against Las Vegas. Milroe has now prepared for that possibility for weeks. Darnold's recovery is undetermined, although Seattle has a Week 11 bye that gives its injured quarterbacks extra time to heal. Milroe's future still depends on the health of the players ahead of him. away.headline: Week 10 Injury Report: Seahawks at Raiders
away.blurb: The Seahawks will be getting a couple of players back from injury for Sunday's game in Las Vegas, with outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu and receiver Rashid Shaheed both ready to return after missing the past two games with ankle and knee injuries, respectively. The Seahawks will still be without four players who also missed last week's game: left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (ribs/quadriceps), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), all of whom were ruled out on Friday's injury report. Cross, who was able to practice Thursday on a limited basis, should be able to make it back after Seattle's Week 11 bye, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. Quarterback Drew Lock was limited all week due to elbow and oblique injuries, as was expected coming into the week, but he has no injury designation, and the plan is still for him to make his second straight start in place of Darnold. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed , who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a personal matter, was back at practice Friday and will play, Macdonald said, clarifying that it was a good personal matter. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and receiver Dont'e Thornton (back), are listed as questionable. Thursday's report featured only a couple of changes for the Seahawks, including a significant one for the offensive line, with left tackle Charles Cross , who has missed the past two games with an ankle injury, listed as limited after not practicing Wednesday. The only other changes were that tight end AJ Barner , who was a full participant Wednesday with a finger injury, has been removed from the injury report altogether, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who got a rest day on Wednesday, was a full participant. As expected, quarterback Drew Lock was limited again, as has been the plan as he prepares to start while dealing with elbow and oblique injuries. Receiver Rashid Shaheed , who is trying to make his way back from a knee injury that kept him out of two games, was a full participant for the second day in a row, while Uchenna Nwosu , who is trying to get back from an ankle injury, was limited for the second day in a row. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who is dealing with a stinger, was a non-participant for the second day in a row, as were quarterback Sam Darnold and left guard Quenton Nelson , both of whom have already been ruled out of Week 10 by Mike Macdonald. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back) was upgraded from limited to full participation, while defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn (concussion) were limited for the second straight day. The Seahawks kicked off their practice week on Wednesday ahead of a Week 10 road matchup against the Raiders, and saw a couple of players who missed Sunday's win over the Cardinals return to the practice field. home.headline: Week 10 Injury Report: Seahawks at Raiders
home.blurb: The Seahawks will be getting a couple of players back from injury for Sunday's game in Las Vegas, with outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu and receiver Rashid Shaheed both ready to return after missing the past two games with ankle and knee injuries, respectively. The Seahawks will still be without four players who also missed last week's game: left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (ribs/quadriceps), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), all of whom were ruled out on Friday's injury report. Cross, who was able to practice Thursday on a limited basis, should be able to make it back after Seattle's Week 11 bye, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. Quarterback Drew Lock was limited all week due to elbow and oblique injuries, as was expected coming into the week, but he has no injury designation, and the plan is still for him to make his second straight start in place of Darnold. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed , who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a personal matter, was back at practice Friday and will play, Macdonald said, clarifying that it was a good personal matter. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and receiver Dont'e Thornton (back), are listed as questionable. Thursday's report featured only a couple of changes for the Seahawks, including a significant one for the offensive line, with left tackle Charles Cross , who has missed the past two games with an ankle injury, listed as limited after not practicing Wednesday. The only other changes were that tight end AJ Barner , who was a full participant Wednesday with a finger injury, has been removed from the injury report altogether, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who got a rest day on Wednesday, was a full participant. As expected, quarterback Drew Lock was limited again, as has been the plan as he prepares to start while dealing with elbow and oblique injuries. Receiver Rashid Shaheed , who is trying to make his way back from a knee injury that kept him out of two games, was a full participant for the second day in a row, while Uchenna Nwosu , who is trying to get back from an ankle injury, was limited for the second day in a row. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who is dealing with a stinger, was a non-participant for the second day in a row, as were quarterback Sam Darnold and left guard Quenton Nelson , both of whom have already been ruled out of Week 10 by Mike Macdonald. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back) was upgraded from limited to full participation, while defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn (concussion) were limited for the second straight day.
