home.headline: Seahawks Week 10 injury report vs. Raiders: Leonard Williams injury is good news for Fernando Mendoza
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Leonard Williams against the Las Vegas Raiders , removing a major defensive obstacle for Fernando Mendoza ahead of his first NFL start. Williams missed every practice this week with a stinger and was officially ruled out Friday, leaving Seattle to adjust its defensive front for Sunday's matchup. His absence is one of four confirmed setbacks for the Seahawks. Quarterback Sam Darnold, left tackle Charles Cross and guard Quenton Nelson are also out, creating challenges on both sides of the ball as Seattle heads to Las Vegas. Williams' recovery has not progressed enough for a return to contact. Head coach Mike Macdonald explained Friday that the defensive tackle can move around and maintain his conditioning, but the injury remains an obstacle to playing. Seattle, however, views the unfamiliar quarterback as a preparation challenge of its own. Defensive tackle Byron Murphy II noted the limited professional film available on Mendoza while emphasizing that the rookie can make every throw. Murphy stressed coordinated pressure and communication as priorities. The Seahawks received encouraging news elsewhere up front. Uchenna Nwosu progressed from two limited sessions to full participation Friday and carries no game designation. Brandon Pili also returned to full work after missing Wednesday and Thursday with a back injury, providing available depth without replacing Williams' individual impact. Darnold missed all three practices with rib and quadriceps injuries. Drew Lock is expected to start again despite managing right elbow and oblique issues. Lock remained limited throughout the week but received no game designation. Protecting him becomes more complicated without Cross and Nelson. Cross briefly returned for limited work Thursday before sitting out Friday with his ankle injury. Nelson did not practice all week because of his knee issue. Anthony Bradford offered better news, advancing to full participation Friday after two limited sessions. Derick Hall missed Friday after two limited sessions with a back injury, but he also carries no game designation. That distinction leaves Seattle with four confirmed absences and no additional players officially listed as questionable. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. home.headline: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
home.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. home.headline: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals
home.blurb: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals The Los Angeles Rams will be managing several injuries on Sunday as they take on the Arizona Cardinals for the second time this season in Week 10. While wide receiver Puka Nacua went on injured reserve this week , left guard Steve Avila has been ruled out as well. Additionally, after making his return in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders, Myles Garrett has officially been listed as questionable but is expected to play, according to head coach Sean McVay. In addition to Garrett, tight end Davis Allen, long snapper Joe Cardona, cornerback Trent McDuffie, and safety Kam Curl were all listed as questionable. After being a non-participant in practice on Thursday, Allen was limited in Friday's practice. With Colby Parkinson not having an injury designation, the Rams should be in a good spot at tight end if Allen is able to go. More importantly, the Rams will be looking to get McDuffie back in action. He was a non-participant in practice on Thursday but was upgraded to limited on Friday. After returning against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8, McDuffie missed last week's game against the Commanders and has been nursing a back injury. "A lot of it is going to be contingent upon how that limited work goes today. He was rolling, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday," McVay said. "He's chomping at the bit to play, but a lot of that answer will be predicated on how he handles the physical workload today. I think if you asked him, he would say that he's hopeful to be able to play and so are we, but that could change based on how the workout goes." Without Nacua on Sunday, the Rams will be relying heavily on their wide receiver depth . The Rams signed Xavier Smith back to the roster this week and also added Brennan Presley to the active roster. With Avila out as well, Beaux Limmer will likely take his spot at left guard. While the Rams are hoping to get McDuffie back, if he is out, the Rams will rely on Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace for a second straight week. On the Cardinals' side of things, defensive lineman Zach Carter, center Hjalte Froholdt, and interior offensive lineman Jon Gaines have all been ruled out. Additionally, tight end Hunter Long, cornerback Max Melton, offensive lineman Jayden Williams, safety Andrew Wingard, defensive lineman Roy Lopez, and defensive lineman Darius Robinson are all questionable. picks.blurb: Expert predictions for Cowboys-49ers: Can Dallas climb to .500 with a huge upset? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) throws an incomplete pass to wide receiver Michael Gallup as he's pressured by San Francisco 49ers defensive end Drake Jackson (95) during the first quarter at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California, October 8, 2023. (Tom Fox/Dallas Morning News) SportsDay Staff · Dallas Morning News Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will the Cowboys finally be able to climb back to .500 and pick up their first marquee win of the season? They'll have a massive opportunity to do just that Sunday when the San Francisco 49ers come to AT&T Stadium as the two teams renew their historic rivalry . Dallas enters the game with a 4-5 record and, after the Commanders' win over the Giants on Thursday, a chance to climb even with New York in the win column. Meanwhile, San Francisco enters the game with a 7-1 record and has quickly established itself as one of the NFL's Super Bowl favorites. Can the Cowboys pull off an upset and get their season back on track? The Dallas Morning News ' columnists and beat writers gave their predictions below. Tim Cowlishaw The good news for Dallas is the 49ers can't really take advantage of the Cowboys' challenged secondary because of their injury troubles at wide receiver. The bad news is the 49ers can take advantage of everything else. A team that plays with grit despite its current 7-1 record, San Francisco figures to dominate time of possession with its multi-pronged running attack, and it will take some huge plays from Dak Prescott against the league's No. 3 defense to keep the Cowboys engaged for long in this one. The recipe is there for a Cowboys loss. The Cowboys haven't pieced together back-to-back wins in nearly a year, despite many opportunities along the way. The 49ers might be the class of the NFC, with an offense that continues to score, despite a ton of injuries, and a defense that is as fast as it is physical. Will this be the week the Cowboys finally stack two wins in a row? It's unlikely. 49ers 35, Cowboys 28 You won't find many (any?) realistic NFL fans giving the Cowboys a shot to win this week. Any path to victory would include the 49ers making self-inflicted mistakes and Dallas' offense playing flawlessly. Yes, the Cowboys' offense performs much better at AT&T Stadium, but it still disappears for long stretches during games. Even Brandon Aubrey has struggled to find his range of late. The red-clad fans will have plenty to cheer for in Arlington. Abraham Nudelstejer Given what we've seen this season, this is probably the easiest prediction to make so far. The Cowboys already have lost at home to a team whose season is all but over, and to another that could still reach the playoffs only because of the woeful state of its division. There is no tangible evidence of improvement that would justify picking Dallas to beat a squad that, with just one loss all year, appears destined to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl. The best Dallas can realistically hope for is to put up a spirited fight and begin preparing for next week's game. 49ers 34, Cowboys 13 Kevin Sherrington Jerry Jones did the right thing by not mortgaging any more of his future to try to save this season, and this game against the 49ers should do nothing but affirm that decision. The Cowboys won't hang 500 yards on the 49ers like they did the Colts. San Francisco has the third-best defense in the NFL, meaning Dak Prescott can't hope to outscore them. 49ers 31, Cowboys 24 Calvin Watkins If the postseason started today, the 49ers would be the No. 1 seed. The Cowboys? Well, you know what's happening with them. If the Cowboys want to get back into the playoff chase, and that's winning the NFC East, beating the 49ers is a good start. It's a difficult task considering how good the 49ers are on defense (ranked third in total defense) so the Cowboys' offense will have to be near-perfect. That's hard to do. The 49ers should handle things. 49ers 30, Cowboys 17 This article originally published at Expert predictions for Cowboys-49ers: Can Dallas climb to .500 with a huge upset? .

away.headline: NFL executive has concerning prediction for 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey
away.blurb: McCaffrey carries no game designation for Sunday’s matchup with the Dallas Cowboys. He sat out Wednesday for rest, then practiced fully Thursday and Friday. Related Articles What George Pickens’ Bizarre Answer Means for His Cowboys Return vs. 49ers Texans Hit With Major Injury Blow as 4 Key Starters Ruled Out Against Browns San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has scored 10 touchdowns through eight games, helping his team build a 7-1 record. One NFL executive still expects the 49ers to need more from rookie running back Kaelon Black before the season ends. The executive’s praise for Black came with a prediction about McCaffrey getting injured. “He’s an explosive runner,” an NFC executive told ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler of Black, adding that “Christian [McCaffrey] will undoubtedly get hurt at some point.” Fowler included the comment in a Friday report on the NFL’s playoff races and emerging players. The executive was not identified and did not offer a reason for the injury prediction. The 30-year-old has appeared in all eight of San Francisco’s games this season. He leads the team with 457 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns, adding 36 catches for 270 yards and another score. Only tight end George Kittle has more receptions for the 49ers. Kaelon Black earns work alongside Christian McCaffrey Black has already become a regular part of coach Kyle Shanahan’s offense. He has 68 carries for 303 yards and a touchdown, averaging 4.5 yards per attempt. His 133 rushing yards over the past two games include a 30-yard touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons. In last Sunday’s 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Black carried 11 times for 70 yards. McCaffrey had 18 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, along with two catches for 19 yards and another score. That gave San Francisco 138 rushing yards from its top two backs, with Black accounting for more than a third of their combined carries. The rookie also handled double-digit rushing attempts in the season opener against the Los Angeles Rams, finishing with 65 yards on 14 carries. McCaffrey’s workload remains below last season’s pace. He finished the 2025 regular season with 311 carries and 102 receptions across 17 starts, totaling 2,126 yards from scrimmage and 17 touchdowns. He won the AP Comeback Player of the Year award. Through eight games this year, McCaffrey has 138 touches for 727 yards from scrimmage. His receiving role remains far larger than Black’s, who has three catches for four yards. home.blurb: That is going to continue when the 49ers are on the sidelines in Dallas to take on the Cowboys. The Niners and Cowboys remain traditional rivals even if the Cowboys are decades away from the time they went head-to-head with the 49ers for NFC honors. Look for the Niners to come out with one of their best efforts at AT&T Stadium. In addition to Evans’ status, the most concerning Niners injury on the offensive side of the ball concern OT Trent Williams. He has a shoulder issue that limited him during the team’s Thursday practice and did not allow him to participate Friday. He is a 12-time Pro Bowl left tackle and if he can’t play, that’s a huge blow for the offense. If he can play but is unable to compete at the highest level, it will make it very difficult for Purdy to feel comfortable in the pocket. On the defensive side, linebacker Dre Greenlaw has been listed as questionable with a knee injury. Greenlaw is second on the team in tackles with 57 stops. He also had 3 tackles for loss while forcing 1 fumble and recovering another. Cornerback Renardo Green has a back issue and he is also considered questionable. Green has 30 tackles, 6 passes defensed and a team-leading 4 interceptions. He has a chance to be a very valuable weapon if he can hunt down an interception against Cowboys QB Dak Prescott. Green is not the only member of the secondary with an injury issue. CB Deommodore Lenoir is questionable with a foot injury while nickel back Upton Stout has shoulder and neck issues and is also listed as questionable. The San Francisco 49ers have the best record in the NFC through their first eight games, but there is no satisfaction in the 49ers locker room just because the Niners have a 7-1 record. They have a significant 2.5-game lead in the NFC West over the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and the Los Angeles Rams, but head coach Kyle Shanahan continues to push his team hard. The 49ers have a powerful and versatile team and they are led by QB Brock Purdy and RB Christian McCaffrey. However, their wide receiver crew will not be at full strength because Mike Evans’ Achilles injury will not allow him to play in this game. As a result, the 49ers are going to work new acquisition Keenan Allen into the lineup in an attempt to get some juice from the WR position. While the Niners have been doing the little things to win games, they are not getting much from their wide receivers other than Evans, and he is clearly sidelined for this game. In addition to his size and skill, Evans sets the tone for the other receivers on the team, and his injury pushed the Niners into acquiring Allen to help the receiving crew. home.headline: NFL expert sheds light on trade calls for Dallas Cowboys star George Pickens
home.blurb: The absence of inquiries highlighted how little momentum existed behind the trade rumors. While several teams explored ways to strengthen their receiving groups before the deadline, the market was not focused on acquiring high-end talent. That limited demand made a potential deal involving Pickens unlikely from the beginning. The Dallas Cowboys never received trade calls for wide receiver George Pickens before the NFL deadline , according to ESPN reporter Jeremy Fowler. Despite speculation about his availability, the organization had no intention of moving the receiver, who was reportedly happy with his situation and did not want to leave Dallas. Fowler reported that teams searching for wide receiver help were not shopping at the premium end of the market. Clubs appeared more interested in finding affordable additions rather than pursuing an expensive or high-profile option. As a result, the Cowboys had no reason to expect significant interest in a player they already wanted to keep. Pickens also worked against the possibility of a trade. Pickens was reportedly comfortable in Dallas and had no desire to be sent to another team during the season. His position aligned with the organization’s plans, removing another potential factor that could have encouraged the front office to consider moving him before the deadline. NFL Expert Sheds Light on Trade Calls for Dallas Cowboys Star George Pickens As it stands, Pickens didn’t receive a lot of interest right before the deadline. This is detailed more in an analysis by Jeremy Fowler for ESPN. Fowler: The Cowboys did not receive any trade calls on receiver George Pickens, who is happy in Dallas and didn’t want to be traded. Teams in the receiver market weren’t shopping in the high-end aisle, either, so the idea of a Pickens trade was a nonstarter. Plus, Dallas had no plans to deal him. Dallas also had no incentive to initiate discussions or entertain a trade involving one of its receiving options. The lack of incoming calls meant the Cowboys were not forced to evaluate offers or determine whether the proposed compensation justified making a roster change. Instead, the franchise maintained its existing plans and allowed the deadline to pass without a transaction. The situation ultimately showed that the speculation surrounding Pickens was not supported by meaningful trade activity. There were no reported inquiries, no established market for a premium receiver and no willingness from Dallas to move the player. With both the organization and the wideout satisfied with the arrangement, the possibility of a deadline trade never developed into a realistic scenario. ・ Skip Bayless Reacts to Buffalo Bills Win Vs. Shanahan said Evans is making progress, but emphasized the importance of allowing him to fully recover. home.blurb: Mike Evans 'Real Close' to a Return? "Mike's such a dog and wants to get out there all the time. And I think it'd be hard to keep him out if this was the last game or anything like that," Shanahan explained . "But what we're trying not to do is have him come back and then be out right away. We're trying to build him up the right way, so hopefully, it can last a little bit." NFL Network's Mike Garafolo said on Nov. 8 that Evans was "questionable at best" for the Cowboys game. He also compared the injury to the Achilles tendinitis that sidelined Christian McCaffrey two seasons ago. That's a big bounce back for a player who was limited to eight games in his final season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of a hamstring injury and a broken collarbone. He finished that year with 30 catches, 368 yards and three touchdowns. The 49ers have split their two games without him. They lost for the first time this season to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. Then they came out of the bye and beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on the strength of five second-half takeaways. Second-year wideout Jordan Watkins made one of the plays of that game with a leaping 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, all with Deebo Samuel also out. Samuel was limited in practice this week with a hamstring injury. That means Brock Purdy could be missing both of his top receivers again when the 49ers take on a Cowboys defense that has given up 236 points in nine games . Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh. Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown. Where to watch Bengals vs. Steelers live When: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Where: Paycor Stadium -- Cincinnati, Ohio TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3.5, O/U 47.5 (via DraftKings ) Bengals vs. Steelers: Need to know Last time we met The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-27 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. Reasons for success Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally. Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe . Prediction, pick This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night. In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Pittsburgh always seems to be right in the thick of it in these division games, and the first matchup was decided by only three points. I think the scoring margin is the same here, but with slightly lower scoring, in keeping with the trend of divisional rematches. … Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 20 Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) (MNF) Dajani ( Chargers +4.5): This is potentially the worst Monday night game of all time. A winless team that hasn't covered the spread since last year vs. a spiraling team starting a new quarterback. Jacoby Brissett is an upgrade over Joe Fagnano , but how much of an upgrade immediately? I don't have a great read on this matchup, but I'll take Jim Harbaugh to keep things close with his brother's old team. … Prediction: Ravens 20, Chargers 17 Dubin (Chargers +4.5): I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. … Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20 Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Da

AFC North rivals put their winning streaks on the line when the Cincinnati Bengals host the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. Cincinnati is on a four-game run, coming off a one-sided win in Spain last weekend, laying just over a field goal at Paycor Stadium. Pittsburgh enjoyed a bye in Week 9 and hopes that break didn't kill the momentum of its own four-game streak. Early Steelers vs Bengals spread pick: Steelers +3.5 No division does rivalry like the AFC North. Regardless of record, this group always seems to compete against each other. The Pittsburgh Steelers drew first blood against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. They won a 30-27 shootout as 3.5-point home underdogs. That kicked off a 4-1 SU and ATS run for Pittsburgh. The Steelers have tightened the bolts on their defense during this successful stretch, entering Week 10 among the Top 10 in marquee analytics like Defensive DVOA and EPA allowed per play . This is arguably the best stop unit the Bengals have faced during their four-game streak, in which Cincy has sliced up opponents to rate as the No. 1 attack in EPA per play since Week 5. That said, the Bengals have a daunting turnaround after playing in Spain last Sunday, and it looks like this spread is growing with some markets showing Cincinnati -4. Sunday Night Football is a fight between four-game winning streaks, with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals adding another chapter to their AFC North rivalry. Both sides come into Week 10 on red-hot runs, but Pittsburgh boasts a rest advantage in Week 10. The Steelers are coming off a bye, while Cincinnati had to travel to Spain and back ahead of this prime-time showdown. Despite the quick turnaround, the Bengals are installed as 3.5-point favorites at Paycor Stadium. My Steelers vs. Bengals prediction sizes up those streaks, giving my favorite NFL picks for SNF on Nov. 15. TOP Pick Steelers vs Bengals prediction: Steelers +3.5 If you take in my NFL Underdogs column each week, you'll note that I'm taking the points with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night. Outside of that rest edge, Pittsburgh presents a stiff test for this high-octane Cincinnati Bengals offense. Cincinnati has strung together four wins, all while piling up 146 total points, but doing so against some softer stop units. During this stretch, the Bengals have beaten up on defenses ranked 22nd or worse in EPA allowed per play since Week 5 . The Steelers, on the other hand, have only gotten stronger on that side of the ball. Pittsburgh took time to adapt to new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham after running Mike Tomlin's playbook forever. And Graham needed time to adjust his plans to the personnel. We've seen this unit really come together during the Steelers' respective four-game streak, jumping into the Top 5 in several key defensive metrics, including flipping their opponents' success rate per play from 46% to 38.7% since Week 5. These AFC North rivalries are always tight, and I like Pittsburgh getting a FG or more on SNF. Steelers vs Bengals combo Pittsburgh has the defensive prowess and ball-hogging run game to take the air out of the Bengals' high-flying attack. The Steelers covered as a dog versus Cincy in Week 3 and are 9-3 ATS in their last dozen games catching points from their AFC North foe. Chase Brown almost snapped his touchdown drought last week in Spain but had a receiving score called back. His TD forecasts sit around 50% for Week 10, with Brown a threat to run or catch for six points. Mike Gesicki has posted 37, 53, and 68 yards versus the rival Steelers in his time with Cincinnati. With Burrow forced to check down more, the tight end sees plenty of work, and his projections sit as high as 39+ yards on SNF. The Bengals running back hasn't scored since Week 1 and had a receiving TD called back in Week 9's win over Atlanta. Cincinnati's passing attack has been so effective that Brown hasn't seen many red-zone opportunities. But with Pittsburgh posing a tougher defensive test, the Bengals may need to grind out yards inside the 20. Brown is a great buy-low option in the touchdown markets, with his pricing trimmed significantly. Forecasts still give him around a 50% shot of finally finding paydirt on SNF . Instead, I'm taking Rico Dowdle to score, just like he did before the bye when he got his first of the season. That was his third game back from injury, and the team leaned heavily on him, giving him 15 carries. Dowdle isn't as efficient as Warren, or as dangerous in the open field, but he's better between the tackles and earning those hard yards , which is why his role will continue to grow and he'll vulture some of Warren's goal-line carries. They are actually level in rushing attempts inside the 10 , and with increased usage, he's the smartest value play for the Steelers on SNF. Bengals touchdown pick: Ja'Marr Chase To say Ja'Marr Chase is playing well is an understatement, and he's without a doubt the best player to back for scoring on Sunday. He's been on the field constantly, running a route on 97% of the team's dropbacks last week, and he has an elite target-per-route run percentage of 39% , with Joe Burrow looking for him at every opportunity. He's now scored seven touchdowns in eight games and found the end zone in his last four appearances. Not to mention that he scored when these teams met in Week Three, with an impressive 98-yard day. He also leads the team in red zone targets, nearly double those of Tee Higgins: 13 to seven. First touchdown scorer pick: Chase Brown The numbers don't look good at first glance for Chase Brown , with just one touchdown all season, which came all the way back in Week One, but I urge you to look past that. Positive regression is coming his way because he's been very efficient lately. Last week, he finished with +11 rushing yards over expected . Samaje Perine doesn't look like much of a factor either; even if he had an increased workload last week, he simply isn't as efficient. The Steelers' run defense is good, but with Burrow playing at MVP levels and the passing game thriving, it might open the box slightly, giving Brown some chances. Long-shot touchdown pick: Joe Burrow As much as I think Brown will score on Sunday, I can't help but think it's his quarterback who offers the best long shot on the board. We've seen the Cincinnati Bengals QB pick up three rushing touchdowns this season , including one TD in each of the past weeks. He's had five rushing attempts inside the 10 this season, which doesn't sound like much, but it's one more than Perine, who is a 29% chance to score, and only three less than Brown, who is nearly a pick'em. Steelers vs Bengals touchdown combo The Chase-Higgins combination is arguably the best receiving duo in football, and they've already racked up 13 touchdowns this season. In eight games, they've had four games in which they've both found the end zone. With Burrow continuing to put up great numbers, I'm keen to back them finding the end zone together again, much like they did when they played the Steelers in Week Three. picks.blurb: Pickswise - Expert Sports Picks & Predictions NFL NCAAF NBA NHL NCAAB UFC More Sports News Betting Casino Playzone Get App Bonuses Home Steelers vs Bengals Same Game Parlay: Best SGP Picks Table of Contents Bengals ML (-180) Over 49.5 (-108) Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) and to score a touchdown (+120) Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season continues with Sunday Night Football between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. It is huge matchup in the AFC North, where everyone is still in contention. These two teams are currently tied at the top with twin 6-2 records. Here is my SGP for Sunday’s primetime festivities, which get underway at 8:20 pm ET on NBC. Also be sure to check out our full Steelers vs Bengals predictions . Bengals ML (-180) Over 49.5 (-108) Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) Tee Higgins to score a touchdown (+120) Parlay odds: +625 Part of the value in a Same Game Parlay, of course, is that all of its components can be correlated if you so choose. That is the entire plan here, as Cincinnati receiver Tee Higgins having a big night would obviously work well with a win by the Bengals and plenty of points being scored. Let’s break down each of the three legs. Pittsburgh prevailed 30-27 in the first head-to-head showdown on September 27, but I’m not too concerned. The Steelers have swept the Bengals in a regular-season series only once since 2019. Aaron Rodgers’ squad overachieved in the first half of this season, but the first nine weeks were hardly convincing. Cincinnati, on the other hand, was mightily impressive en route to its six victories. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are looking unstoppable. Even the defense has become an average unit – and average means good by the Bengals’ standards on that side of the ball. I’m not willing to give more than a field goal in this AFC North rivalry matchup (or really in any game involving two teams from this division), but the Bengals should be able to win it outright. This correlates nicely with the Bengals on the money line. After all, you can be almost certain that a whole bunch of points will be scored if the game is played at Cincinnati’s pace. Pittsburgh, of course, would much rather play more of a defensive slog. The first meeting between these two teams in 2026 resulted in 57 points, obviously an encouraging sign for another over on Sunday. The Bengals have not slowed down, either. In fact, they have only been getting better and better. Burrow and company have put 31, 35, 43 and 34 points on the board in their last four outings. Although Cincy’s defense has stepped up in recent weeks, keep in mind that this is a unit that got torched for 36 points by the lowly Titans earlier this month. The Bengals also watched the Steelers churn out 7.0 yards per play in this season’s first head-to-head matchup. Cincinnati ranks dead last in the entire NFL in opponents’ yards per rush (5.0), so Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren can be expected to go borderline crazy in this one. He turned 17 attempts into 127 yards against Cincy earlier this year. Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) and to score a touchdown (+120) Higgins has been on a heater of late – and really this entire season. The Clemson product has caught 48 of 67 targets for 758 yards and six touchdowns. He has produced at least 148 yards in three of the last five games and has scored five touchdowns in the past three weeks. Yes – five touchdowns in the past three weeks. Burrow is playing like an MVP candidate (if not even the favorite) and Chase always demands a ton of attention from opposing defenses. Elite cornerback Jamel Dean will likely be on Chase for the most part, which means things could open up for Higgins. When these two teams faced each other back in Week 3, Higgins made six receptions on seven targets for 90 yards and one TD. away.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . Chargers vs Ravens prediction: Under 38.5 Not only are the Chargers 0-7-1 ATS this year, but they're also 6-2 to the Under, with their opponents scoring 44 and 30 points in those two Overs. They were already one of the slowest-paced teams , per THE BLITZ, but could be even slower in and out of the huddle with a new voice. The Chargers are already the worst-scoring offense in football , and Ladd McConkey didn't practice on Thursday and missed last week. Even when the Chargers have to turn up the pass rate when trailing, Justin Herbert is getting taken down. Herbert is among the NFL's most-sacked quarterbacks and went down eight times last week while trying to rally against Houston. It's a preseason total, but will the Baltimore offense look that much different than Week 9 TNF? The Chargers could be changing starters on the O-line as well, adding to the pressure. Hampton led the backfield with 13 carries last week in a blowout loss , while Keaton Mitchell's fumble could eat into his 25% workload. Pairing the TD prop with Under 38.5 boosts the overall price. This has the makings of a slow, run-first game, with pressure on Justin Herbert and the Chargers' struggling offensive line potentially keeping them behind the sticks all night. LA is the lowest-scoring unit in football, ranks second-last in red-zone opportunities per game and has the fourth-worst red-zone TD rate. Add in an offensive line allowing 3.9 sacks per game (second-most in the NFL), coming off an eight-sack performance against Houston, and potentially facing personnel changes, and Baltimore might not need to throw much at all Monday night. away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

home.headline: New Lamar Jackson Rumors Update When Ravens QB Had Surgery amid Latest Injury Timeline for Return
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season." Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson's surgery happened last week so based on the estimated recovery time of six to 10 weeks, he could potentially be back on the field before the regular season ends. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Nov. 13 that Jackson's recovery timeline was "challenging to predict" after he underwent surgery to address a dislocated and broken right thumb. A six-week recovery would have Jackson back around Week 15 when the Ravens play the Pittsburgh Steelers. The full 10-week timeline would give him a chance to play in Week 18, also against the Steelers. In addition to his hand injury, Jackson also missed three games earlier in the year after suffering a high ankle sprain. In five games, he played just 14 full quarters and threw for 961 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and another score. In the wake of Jackson's injury, the Ravens traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to make his first start for the team against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. At 4-5, Baltimore has work to do if it hopes to make the playoffs. The Ravens will likely remain cautious with Jackson's recovery, making the acquisition of Brissett a critical move as they look to snap their four-game losing streak going into Monday night.

home.headline: NFL fans question Ravens' handling of Lamar Jackson injury news, point finger at Eric DeCosta
home.blurb: Jackson has not played since hurting his thumb on Baltimore’s opening offensive snap against the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. He has since undergone surgery, which will keep him out for six to 10 weeks. In his absence, the Ravens will turn to veteran Jacoby Brissett, whom they acquired in a recent trade with the Arizona Cardinals. “Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return,” his statement read. They aren’t entirely out of the playoff picture, but losing Jackson for an extended stretch certainly hurts their chances. Baltimore will look to snap its losing streak Monday night against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. The Baltimore Ravens are in a tough spot. They have lost four games in a row after racing to a 4-1 start, and now Lamar Jackson is set to miss extended time with a thumb injury. Off the field, Jesse Minter has drawn criticism since the Jackson news broke. Fans across the football world took issue with how the head coach handled questions about the QB’s injury, and some said his answers sounded just like John Harbaugh. Fans Mock Jesse Minter, Compare Him to John Harbaugh On Friday, the Ravens announced that Jackson’s recovery timeline would be six to 10 weeks. Minter met with the media Saturday to discuss the situation further, but when pressed for a timeline on the surgery, he was vague with his answer. “The surgery happened, and the timeline is the timeline,” Minter said , via ESPN’s Jamison Hensley. Fans had a field day with the response, and some even likened Minter to his predecessor. “The Ravens fired John Harbaugh and hired… John Harbaugh,” one fan wrote , adding a laughing emoji. Some fans saw a bigger problem in how the Ravens handle injury news, and one pointed the finger at the front office. “Remember when fans would blast Harbaugh for being coy about a player being injured? Like it was all his idea/personality? Minter is doing the same thing, so this points directly to Eric DeCosta,” another said . One fan was more direct, calling Minter’s press conference “highly unusual.” “This is objectively bizarre and highly unusual,” they remarked . “Why are they being so weird about this?” a fourth fan asked . home.headline: Ravens get devastating update on Lamar Jackson’s status
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens offered a clearer picture of Lamar Jackson’s recovery Friday but stopped short of setting a return date for their franchise quarterback. “Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Jackson injured his throwing hand on Baltimore’s first offensive play against Buffalo on November 1. His right hand struck Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau as he attempted a throw, immediately ending his return to the lineup. He had already missed three games with an ankle injury. Related Articles Kirk Cousins’ Vikings Return Comes With an Emotional Twist In a statement released by the team, head coach Jesse Minter said injuries like Jackson’s broken and dislocated thumb typically require six to 10 weeks to heal when surgery is necessary. The update leaves Baltimore preparing for an extended stretch without the two-time NFL MVP as it tries to reverse a four-game losing streak. “Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8,” Minter said. Minter described a typical healing window rather than announcing Jackson would miss another six to 10 weeks beginning Friday. The statement did not specify a target game or establish when that recovery window began. The Ravens’ quarterback problems worsened that afternoon when Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the Buffalo game and started the following Thursday against Jacksonville. Baltimore lost those games 36-10 and 33-10, respectively, falling to 4-5. Following the loss, the Ravens made a trade to acquire Jacoby Brissett from Arizona on November 6. The veteran is preparing to make his first Baltimore start Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) while learning a new offense on an accelerated schedule. “It’s definitely a crash course. No question,” Brissett said Thursday. Baltimore has scored no more than 13 points in any game during its four-game skid. Brissett’s immediate assignment is to restore enough offensive consistency to stop that slide. Jackson has not abandoned the possibility of returning this season. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport previously reported that he told teammates he intended to come back, although his recovery and Baltimore’s ability to remain competitive will shape that possibility. The Ravens need to keep their season alive while Jackson recovers. That responsibility now falls to Brissett, whose first start Monday offers Baltimore a chance to end its four-game skid and give its injured quarterback something to come back to.
